dedoceo.definition: dē-doceō ēre, uī, ctus, to cause to unlearn, unteach, teach the opposite of: aliquem geometriam: (virtus) populum falsis Dedocet uti Vocibus, H.: cum a Zenone fortis esse didicisset, a dolore dedoctus est: ut coercend…

dedoleo.definition: de-doleō uī, ēre, to cease grieving, O.

deduco.definition: dē-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere (imper. deduc, C.; deduce, T.), to lead away, draw out, turn aside, divert, bring out, remove, drive off, draw down: atomos de viā: eum contionari conantem de rostris, drag down, Cs.: aliquem…

deductio.definition: dēductiō ōnis, f deduco, a leading away, conducting off : rivorum a fonte: Albanae aquae. —Of colonists, a leading forth, establishing, colonizing : in istos agros: militum in oppida.—In law, an ejection, expulsion : …

deductus.definition: dēductus adj. P. of deduco, lowered, unambitious, modest (poet.): carmen, V.: vox, Pr.

deerro.definition: de-errō āvī, āre, to wander away, go astray, lose the way: in itinere: caper deerraverat, V.: sors deerrabat ad parum idoneos, fell upon improper persons, Ta.

defatigatio.definition: dēfatīgātiō or dēfetī gātiō ōnis, f defatigo, a wearying, tiring out, weariness, fatigue, exhaustion : membrorum: hostium, Cs.: defetigatione caedere desistere: miseriarum.

defatigo.definition: dē-fatīgō or dēfetīgō āvī, ātus, āre, to weary out, tire, fatigue, exhaust: se, T.: exercitum itineribus, Cs.: opus faciam ut defatiger, T.: diuturnitate belli defatigati, Cs.: iudices: numquam defatigabor ante, quam,…

defectio.definition: dēfectiō ōnis, f deficio, a failing, failure, want, lack, disappearance : virium: animi mei, despondency : solis et lunae, eclipse.—A defection, desertion, rebellion, revolt : facta datis obsidibus, Cs.: in defectione…

defector.definition: defector ōris, m deficio, a deserter, apostate : patris sui, Ta.

defectus1.definition: dēfectus adj. P. of deficio, weak, worn out, enfeebled : defecto poplite labens, O.: corpus, Ta.: amor, O.: annis, Ph.

defectus2.definition: dēfectus ūs, m deficio, a falling away, desertion, revolt : Spartanorum, Cu. — A diminution, failure : aquarum, L. — An obscuration, eclipse : solis, V.—Plur: eius (lunae).

defendo.definition: dēfendō dī, sus, ere, to ward off, repel, avert, keep off : bellum, Cs.: ad defendendos ictūs, Cs.: solis ardores: frigus, H.: vim, Cs.: furorem, V.: crimen, to answer, L.: ignem a tectis, O.: solstitium pecori, V.: a…

defensio.definition: dēfēnsiō ōnis, f defendo, a defending, defence : urbis, Cs.: defensionis locum relinquere: defensionem in novo consilio parare, S.: criminis: contra crimen: causae suae: scripta: pro Cornelio, N.: ad istam orationem b…

defensito.definition: dēfēnsitō āvī, —, āre, freq. defenso, to defend often, practise defending : causas: sententiam.

defenso.definition: dēfēnsō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. defendo, to defend diligently, protect : alios ab hostibus, S.: umeros, O.: sua, Ta.: dum defensamus (sc. armentum), O.: defensantes, the guards , Ta.

defensor.definition: dēfēnsor ōris, m defendo, an averter, protector against : necis: calamitatum.— A defender, protector, advocate : quem defensorem paro, T.: tribuni defensores mei: illius, H.: culpae, apologist , Iu.: iuris: causae: op…

defero.definition: dē-ferō tulī, lātus, ferre, to bring away, carry off, take down, carry, take, remove: quae (dolia) amnis defert, V.: secundo Tiberi deferri, L.: ramalia arida tecto, O.: argentum ad eam, T.: litteras ad Caesarem, Cs.:…

defervesco.definition: dē-fervēscō fervī and ferbuī, —, ere, to cease raging, cool down, be allayed, be assuaged: dum defervescat ira: Sperabam iam defervisse adulescentiam, T.: cum cupiditates deferbuissent: quasi deferverat oratio.

defessus.definition: dēfessus adj. P. of defetiscor, worn out, weary, exhausted : verberando, T.: diuturnitate pugnae, Cs.: volneribus: bello, S.: cum integri defessis succederent, Cs.: Aeneadae, V.: accusatio, effete .

defetiscor.definition: dē-fetīscor fessus, ī, dep., to become tired, grow weary, faint: Neque defetiscar experirier, T.

deficio.definition: dēficiō fēcī, fectus, ere (fut perf. defexit, old form. in L.—Pass., usu. deficior; dēfit, T., Enn. ap. C., V.; dēfierī, T.; dēfīet, L.) de + facio.— Intrans, to withdraw, revolt, desert, fall off : civitates quae def…

defigo.definition: dē-fīgō fīxī, fīxus, ere, to fasten, fix, set, drive, set up, plant: crucem ad civium supplicium defigi iubes: sudes sub aquā, Cs.: asseres in terrā defigebantur, Cs.: sicam in corpore: cultrum in corde, L.: telluri h…

defingo.definition: dē-fingō nxī, —, ere, to disfigure, deface, muddle: Rheni luteum caput, H.

definio.definition: dē-fīniō īvī, ītus, īre, to bound, set bounds to, limit, terminate, define: fundi extremam partem oleae ordine: orbem terrarum (loca): huius generis orationem, bring to an end. — Fig., to limit, define, explain: genus…

definitio.definition: dēfīnītiō ōnis, f definio, a limiting, defining, definition, explanation : hominum et temporum: iudiciorum.

definitivus.definition: dēfīnītīvus adj. definio, definitive, explanatory : constitutio: causa.

definitus.definition: dēfīnītus adj. P. of definio, limited, precise, definite : quaestionum (genus): locus.

defio.definition: (dēfīō) dēfit, etc., rare passive for deficior.

deflagratio.definition: dēflagrātiō ōnis, f deflagro, a burning up, conflagration : futura caeli. — Fig.: deflagrationem Italiae minari, destruction .

deflagro.definition: dēflagrō āvī, ātus, āre, to burn down, be consumed by fire: incensa domus deflagravit: aedes, L.: Fana flammā deflagrata.—Fig., to perish, be destroyed: communi incendio: deflagrare omnia pati, L.: in cinere deflagrat…

deflecto.definition: dē-flectō flēxī, flexus, ere.— Trans, to bend aside, turn away, divert: tela, V.: amnīs in alium cursum: ad Romanos cursum, L.: novam viam, to build the road in another direction, L.—Fig., to turn away, lead astray: l…

defleo.definition: dē-fleō ēvī, ētus, ēre, to weep over, lament, deplore, bewail: meum discessum: haec satis diu defleta sunt: Numam, O.: membra defleta, i. e. the dead, V.: Haec ubi deflevit, uttered this lament, V.

defloresco.definition: dē-flōrēscō ruī, —, ere, to drop blossoms, fade, wither, decay, decline: flos tenui carptus ungui, Ct. —Fig.: deliciae deflorescunt: cum senectā res defloruere, L.

defluo.definition: dē-fluō fluxī, fluxus, ere, to flow down: (Rhenus) in plurīs defluit partīs, Cs.: Defluit saxis umor, H.: in Tiberim Orontes, Iu. — To glide down, slide, fall, descend: iam ipsae defluebant coronae: pedes vestis deflu…

defodio.definition: dē-fodiō fōdī, fossus, ere, to dig deep, dig up, make by digging: specus, V.: terram, H. — To bury, cover with earth: thesaurum defossum esse sub lecto: signum in terram, L.: novaculam in comitio: alqm humo, O.: iacen…

deformatio.definition: dēfōrmātiō ōnis, f 2 deformo, a deforming, disfiguring, defacing : tantae maiestatis, L.

deformis.definition: dē-fōrmis e, adj. with comp. de + forma, misshapen, deformed : deformem esse natum. — Formless, without shape : animae, O.— Unsightly, ugly, hideous, loathsome : qui senes ac deformes erant: iumenta, Cs.: agmen, L.: h…

deformitas.definition: dēfōrmitās ātis, f deformis, ugliness, deformity, hideousness : insignis ad deformitatem puer: in tantā deformitate, L. — Fig., baseness, vileness, turpitude : animi: fugae: ludicra, i. e. the disgrace of appearing on…

deformo1.definition: dē-fōrmō āvī, ātus, āre, to bring into shape, form, depict, describe: quem supra deformavi.

deformo2.definition: dēfōrmō āvī, ātus, āre de + forma, to bring out of shape, deform, disfigure, spoil, mar : deformatus corpore: aerumnis deformatus, S.: voltum, V.: parietes deformatos reliquit.—Fig., to mar, spoil, deteriorate, disgra…

defraudo.definition: dē-fraudō or defrūdō ā vī, ātus, āre, to defraud, overreach, cheat: insuper (me), T.: Suom genium, i. e. by self-denial, T.: alquem ne andabatā quidem: ne brevitas defraudasse aurīs videatur.

defrico.definition: dē-fricō cuī, cātus, āre, to rub off, rub down, rub hard: dentem, O., Ct.—Fig.: sale multo Urbem, i. e. cause to smart, H.

defringo.definition: dēfringō frēgī, frāctus, ere de + frango, to break off, break to pieces : ex arbore plantas, V.: ramum arboris: ferrum summā ab hastā, V.

defrutum.definition: dēfrutum ī, n de + FVR-, must boiled down , V.

defugio.definition: dē-fugiō fūgī, —, ere, to run off, flee away, make an escape: ripa, quo sinistrum cornu defugit, L.: iniurias fortunae defugiendo relinquas, i. e. by death.—Fig., to flee from, shun, avoid, escape from: proelium, Cs.:…

defundo.definition: dēfundō fūdī, fūsus, ere, to pour down, pour out: odorem, V.: vinum, to decant, H.: pelvīs, to empty, Iu. — Esp., in libations: te prosequitur mero Defuso pateris, H.

defungor.definition: dē-fungor fūnctus, ī, to have done with, acquit oneself of, discharge, perform, finish: omni populari concitatione: periculis: honoribus: proelio, L.: unius poenā, L.: laboribus, H.: defuncta corpora vitā, dead, V.: t…

degener.definition: dē-gener is, adj. de + genus, inferior to ancestors, degenerate : Neoptolemum, V.: hi iam degeneres sunt, mixti, L.: dignitate formae, Ta.— Unworthy : patrii non degener oris, i. e. inheriting a father's eloquence , O…

degeneratum.definition: dēgenerātum ī, n P. of degenero, baseness, degeneracy : in aliis, L.

degenero.definition: dēgenerō āvī, ātus, āre degener, to be inferior to ancestors, decline, be degenerate : a vobis: Pandione nata, degeneras! O.: Macedones in Syros degenerarunt, L.—Fig., to fall off, decline, degenerate : ut consuetudo …

dego.definition: dēgō dēgī, —, ere de + ago, of time, to spend, pass : cum uno aetatem, T.: inter feras aetatem: expertem sine crimine vitam, V.: otia in thalamo, Ct.: vita, quae cum virtute degatur: aetatis degendae ratio: laetus deg…

degrandinat.definition: dē-grandinat impers, it stops hailing, O.

degravo.definition: dē - gravō —, ātus, āre, to weigh down, overpower, burden: caput, O.: circumventum cornu, L.: onere degravati, Ph. — Fig., to drag down, burden, incommode: peritos nandi volnera degravant, L.: gremium, O.

degredior.definition: dēgredior gressus, ī, dep. de + gradior, to go down, march down, descend : paulum ex eo loco, Cs.: ex arce, L.: monte, S.: in aequum, Ta.: ad pedes, to alight, dismount , L.

degrunnio.definition: dē - grunniō —, —, īre, to grunt out, do his grunting, Ph.

degusto.definition: dē-gustō āvī, ātus, āre, to taste: inde (sc. de sanguine), S.—Poet.: (lancea) summum degustat volnere corpus, i. e. grazes, V. — Fig., to get as a sample, taste, try, make trial of, test: genus hoc exercitationum: ex …

dehinc.definition: de-hinc (monosyi., V., O.), adv., from this time, henceforth, hereafter, for the future: nunc dehinc spero aeternam inter nos gratiam Fore, T.: ne exspectetis argumentum, for the rest, T.: Tarquinium quācunque dehinc …

dehisco.definition: de-hīscō —, —, ere, to part, divide, split open, gape, yawn: vel tellus mihi dehiscat, V.: terrae dehiscunt, V.: rimis dehiscit cumba, O.: dehiscens intervallis hostium acies, L.

dehonestamentum.definition: dehonestāmentum ī, n dehonesto, that which disfigures, a blemish, disgrace, dishonor : oris, Ta.: nullum insigne, Ta.

dehonesto.definition: de-honestō —, —, āre, to disgrace, dishonor: famam, L.: proavum infami operā, Ta.

dehortor.definition: de-hortor ātus, ārī, dep., to advise to the contrary, dissuade: me: me a vobis, from your cause, S.: me ne darem, T.: plura scribere me, S.

deicio.definition: dēiciō or dēiiciō iēcī, iectus, ere de + iacio, to throw down, hurl down, precipitate, prostrate, raze, fell, cut down, tear down, destroy : alqm de ponte in Tiberim: alqm de saxo (Tarpeio), L.: a cervicibus iugum: se…

deiectio.definition: dēiectiō ōnis, f deicio.—In law, an ejection, dispossession : deiectionem facere.

deiectus1.definition: dēiectus adj. P. of deicio, thrown down ; hence, of places, low, sunken, depressed : loca, Cs. —Fig., cast down, dejected, dispirited : haud deiectus, V.

deiectus2.definition: dēiectus ūs, m deicio, a throwing down, felling, fall : arborum, L.: gravis undarum, O.— A declivity, descent : collis, Cs.—Plur: collis deiectūs habebat, Cs.

deiero.definition: dēierō (not -iūrō), āvī, ātus, āre * dēierus; de + iūs, to take an oath, swear : persancte, T.: neminem tradidisse, etc., N.

deinceps.definition: deinceps (disyl., H.), adv. dein + CAP-.—In space, one after another, in order, in succession : cum deinceps ex primis versuum litteris aliquid conectitur: prima Curene est, ac deinceps duae Syrtes, S.: tres deinceps …

deinde.definition: deinde (in poetry two syll.), or dein (in poetry one syll.), adv. de + locat. suffix -im + demonstr. -de.—In space, then, next, thereafter, thence : via interest perangusta, deinde paulo latior patescit campus, L.: du…

delabor.definition: dē-lābor lapsus, ī, dep., to fall, sink, slip down, glide down, descend: in mare (flumen), H.: medios delapsus in hostīs, V.: gradibus, by the steps, O.: signum de caelo delapsum: de manibus civium delapsa arma: ex eq…

delamentor.definition: dē-lāmentor —, ārī, dep., to lament, bewail: natam ademptam, O.

delasso.definition: dē-lassō —, —, āre, to wear out, tire: Fabium, H.

delatio.definition: dēlātiō ōnis, f de + TAL-, an accusation, denunciation : nominis, an indictment : ne haec mihi delatio detur: socius delationis, Ta.

delator.definition: dēlātor ōris, m de + TAL-, an informer, denouncer : criminum, L.: amici, Iu.: cum plena litora multo Delatore forent, Iu.: maiestatis, of high-treason , Ta.

delectabilis.definition: dēlectābilis e, adj. delecto, delightful, agreeable : cibus, Ta.

delectamentum.definition: dēlectāmentum ī, n delecto, a delight, amusement, sport : sibi me pro delectamento putat, T.: delectamenta puerorum.

delectatio.definition: dēlectātiō ōnis, f delecto, a delighting, delight, pleasure, amusement, satisfaction : nulla alia, T.: oculorum: ridendi: conviviorum: mira in cognoscendo: suae delectationis causā .

delecto.definition: dēlectō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. de + lacio, to allure, attract, delight, charm, please, entertain, interest : haec studia delectant domi volunt delectare poetae, H.: me: delectari multis rebus: imperio, Cs.: criminibu…

delectus1.definition: dēlēctus adj. P. of 1 deligo, picked, choice, select, chosen : legio, Cs.: iuventus, V.: equites, S.: cum delectis tentare omnia, picked men , S.

delegatio.definition: dēlēgātiō ōnis, f delego, an assignment (of debt), substitution : a mancipe.

delego1.definition: dē-lēgō āvī, ātus, āre, to send away, despatch: Pleminium in Tullianum ex senatū s consulto, L.: studiosos Catonis ad illud volumen, refer, N.—To commit, give in charge, confide: nec ancillis delegantur (infantes), Ta…

delenimentum.definition: dēlēnīmentum ī, n delenio, a blandishment, allurement : animis obicere, L.: delenimenta vitiorum, i. e. effeminate luxuries , Ta.

delenio.definition: dē-lēniō īvī, ītus, īre, to soothe, soften, charm, captivate, entice, cajole, fascinate: se donis: milites blande appellando: Midan carmine, O.: instrumento voluptatum militum animos, L.: dolentem, H.: dolorem remedii…

delenitor.definition: dēlēnītor ōris, m delenio, a soother, charmer : cuius (iudicis) orator.

deleo.definition: dēleō ēvī (dēlērat, C.; dē lēsset, L.), ētus, ēre de + LI-, to erase, efface, obliterate, blot out : epistulas: cum tabulas prehendisset, digito legata delevit: Non delenda carmina, H.: tabellas, O.: tabulas, Iu.— In …

deletrix.definition: dēlētrīx īcis, f delco, a destroyer : imperi.

deliberabundus.definition: dēlīberābundus adj. delibero, pondering, reflecting : velut deliberabundus, in a brown study , L.

deliberatio.definition: dēlīberātiō ōnis, f delibero, a deliberation, consultation, consideration : de re p.: haec deliberatio, quemnam, etc.: habet res deliberationem, needs consideration : consili capiendi, upon the measure to be adopted :…

deliberativus.definition: dēlīberātīvus adj. delibero, deliberative : genus (rerum), subjects requiring deliberation : causa.

deliberator.definition: dēlīberātor ōris, m delibero, one who ponders, a delayer : ille, that man of hesitation .

deliberatus.definition: dēlīberātus adj. with comp. P. of delibero, resolved upon, determined : Deliberatā morte ferocior, H.: neque illi quicquam deliberatius fuit quam, etc.

delibero.definition: dē-līberō āvī, ātum, āre de + libra, to weigh well, consider maturely, deliberate, ponder, meditate, take counsel, consult, advise upon : re deliberatā, Cs.: hoc, T.: de summā rerum, Cs.: de bello: quid intersit suā: …

delibo.definition: dē-lībō āvī, ātus, āre, to take, enjoy, pluck, gather: flos delibatus populi, the picked flower: omnīs undique flosculos, cull: novum honorem, L.: oscula, V.: artīs, O.—To take away, detract, subtract, remove: de laud…

delibro.definition: dē-librō —, ātus, āre de + 4 liber, to take off the rind, bark, peel : (arborum) delibratis cacuminibus, Cs.

delibutus.definition: dēlibūtus adj. de + LI-, anointed, besmeared, stained, defiled : medicamentis: capillus: atro cruore, H.—Fig.: gaudio, unctuous with joy , T.

delicate.definition: dēlicātē adv. delicatus, delicately, elegantly, luxuriously : vivere: recubans: odiosa multa fecit, N.

delicatus.definition: dēlicātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of * dēlicō, to clear up, alluring, charming, pleasing, delightful, luxurious, voluptuous : in illo delicatissimo litore: hortuli, Ph.: puerorum comitatus: delicatiores in cantu f…

deliciae.definition: dēliciae ārum, f de + 1 LAC-, a delight, pleasure, charm, allurement, luxury, voluptuousness : deliciarum causā: deliciis diffluentes: longissime a talibus deliciis abesse: amores et hae deliciae quae vocantur, pleasu…

deliciolae.definition: dēliciolae ārum, f dim. deliciae, a darling : nostrae, Tulliola.

delicium.definition: dēlicium ī, n de + 1 LAC-, a sweetheart , Ph.

delictum.definition: dēlīctum ī, n de + LIC-, a fault, offence, trespass, crime, transgression, wrong, defect : delictum admisisse in me, T.: maiore commisso delicto, Cs.: leve: leviora, Ta.: distinctio poenarum ex delicto, Ta.: quo delic…

deligo1.definition: dēligō lēgī, lēctus, ere de + 1 lego, to choose, pick out, select, elect, designate, single out : ad eas res conficiendas deligi, Cs.: quos Romae relinqueres: ex civitate fortissimum quemque: ex legionibus fabros, Cs.…

deligo2.definition: dē-ligō āvī, ātus, āre, to bind together, tie up, bind fast, fetter, make fast: hominem deligari iubet: naviculam ad ripam, Cs.: epistulam ad amentum, Cs.: deligati ad palum iuvenes, L.

delino.definition: (dē-linō) —, litus, ere, to rub off, remove: ex quā (columnā) tectorium delitum sit.

delinquo.definition: dē-linquō līquī, lictus, ere, to fail, be wanting, fall short, trespass, err, commit a fault, do wrong, transgress, offend: quod populi adversus P. R. deliquerunt, L. (old formula): ut condemnaretur filius si pater de…

deliquesco.definition: de-liquēscō licuī, —, ere, to melt away, dissolve, melt: Hyrie flendo delicuit, O.—Fig.: qui nec alacritate futtili gestiens deliquescat.

deliratio.definition: dēlīrātiō ōnis, f deliro, giddiness, silliness, folly, dotage, madness : incredibilis.

deliro.definition: dēlīrō —, —, āre delirus, to be crazy, be deranged, be silly, dote, rave : decipi tam dedecet quam delirare: timore, T.: in extis totam Etruriam delirare: Stertinium deliret acumen, H.: quicquid delirant reges, whatev…

delirus.definition: dēlīrus adj. de + lira, silly, doting, crazy : senex: anus: mater, H.

delitigo.definition: dē-lītigō —, —, āre, to scold, rail: tumido ore, H.

delitisco.definition: dēlitīscō (-ēscō) tuī , —, ere de + latesco, to hide away, conceal oneself, lie hid, lurk : bestiae ut in cubilibus delitiscant: hostes noctu in silvis. Cs.: silvā, O.: ut eo mitteret amicos, qui delitiscerent.— To sk…

delphinus.definition: delphīnus ī (C., H., Iu.), or (poet.) delphīn, īnis (V., O., Pr.), m a dolphin.—The Dolphin, a constellation, O.

delubrum.definition: dēlūbrum ī, n de + 3 LV-, a place of cleansing, temple, shrine, sanctuary : audita ex delubro vox, L.: delubrum eius in oppido dedicaverunt: ex alto delubri culmine, V.: deorum delubra.

deludo.definition: dē-lūdō sī, sus, ere, to play false, mock, deceive, make sport of, delude: in hac re me deludier, T.: deludi vosmet a tribuno patiemini?: dolis me, T.: animum responso, V.: quā (linguā) sum delusa, O.: quae sopitos de…

delumbo.definition: dēlumbō —, —, āre de + lumbus, to enervate, weaken : sententias.

demadesco.definition: de-madēscō maduī, —, ere, to become wet, be moistened, O.

demando.definition: dē-mandō āvī, ātus, āre, to give in charge, intrust, commit: pueri unius curae demandabantur, L.: curam (sauciorum) legatis, L.

demano.definition: dē-mānō —, —, āre, to flow down, glide down, Ct.

demens.definition: dē-mēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup, out of one's senses, insane, demented, mad, raving, foolish, distracted: Adeon est demens? T.: num quis est igitur tam demens, qui, etc.: quid est enim dementius, quam, etc.?: A…

demensum.definition: dēmēnsum ī, n demensus, an allowance, ration (of slaves), T.

dementer.definition: dēmenter adv. demens, foolishly, madly : res tam dementer credita: amoribus uti, O.

dementia.definition: dēmentia ae, f demens, insanity, madness, distraction, folly : ut est Dementia, so mad is he , T.: O hanc dementiam, T.: exspectare ... summae dementiae esse iudicabat, Cs.: per dementiam cuncta agere, S.: quae te dem…

demereo.definition: dē-mereō uī, —, ēre, to deserve well of: Crimine te meo, O.

demereor.definition: dē-mereor itus, ērī, dep., to deserve well of, lay under obligation: beneficio civitatem, L.: dum demeremur, while we try to oblige, Ta.

demergo.definition: dē-mergō sī, sus, ere, to sink, submerge, plunge, dip, immerse, bury: caput: demersis rostris, V.: in Tusci demersus fluminis undis, O.: naves, L.: orbes (of the sun), i. e. to set, O.: dapes in alvum, O. — Fig., to p…

demetior.definition: (dē-mētior) mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure off, measure out.—Only P. perf.: verba verbis quasi demensa.

demeto.definition: dē-metō messuī, messus, ere, to mow, reap, cut off, gather, crop, harvest: tempora demetendis fructibus accommodata: demesso frumento, Cs.: alienos agros: pollice florem, to pluck, V.: huic ense caput, to behead, O.

demigratio.definition: dēmigrātiō ōnis, f demigro, an emigration , N.

demigro.definition: dē-migrō āvī, ātus, āre, to migrate, emigrate, move, depart, remove, go away: ex his aedificiis, Cs.: in urbem ex agris, L.: in alias terras: ad Marcellum: aliquo: hinc, i. e. to die: demigrandi causā, Cs.: ex hominum…

deminuo.definition: dē-minuō uī, ūtus, ere, to make smaller, lessen, diminish: deminutae copiae, Cs.: militum vires inopia frumenti deminuerat, Cs.: de bonis, i. e. to alienate in part: praedia. — Fig., to take away, abate, lessen, reduc…

deminutio.definition: dēminūtiō (dīm-) ōnis, f deminuo, a diminution, decrease, lessening, abatement : luminis: civium: vectigalium: de bonis privatorum: provinciae, of the term of office .—In law: datio deminutio, the right of alienation,…

demiror.definition: dē-mīror —, ārī, dep., to wonder, be amazed: (haec vos) sperasse me consule adsequi posse demiror: hoc, qui potueris, etc., I cannot imagine, T.: Quid sit, etc., T.: cur, etc.

demisse.definition: dēmissē adv. with comp. and sup. demissus, low : demissius volabat, O. — Fig., humbly, modestly, abjectly, meanly : sentire: haec demississime exponit, Cs.

demissio.definition: dēmissiō ōnis, f demitto, a letting down, sinking, lowering : storiarum, Cs.—Fig., dejection : animi.

demissus.definition: dēmissus adj. with comp. P. of demitto.— Of places, lowered, sunken, low-lying, low : loca, Cs. — Drooping, falling, hanging down, low : Demissis umeris esse, T.: labia, T.: si demissior ibis, fly too low , O.: demiss…

demitigo.definition: dē-mītigō —, —, āre, to make mild: cottidie demitigamur, grow more lenient.

demitto.definition: de-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to send down, let down, drop, lower, put down, let fall, sink: lacrimas, shed, V.: ubera, let down, V.: ancilia caelo demissa, L.: latum clavum pectore, H.: Maiā genitum demittit ab alto, V…

demo.definition: dēmō dēmpsī, dēmptus, ere de+emo, to take away, take off, subtract, remove, withdraw : haec (epistula) ad turrim adhaesit ... dempta ad Ciceronem defertur, Cs.: semper alqd demendo: Caudae unum (pilum), H.: aurum sibi…

demolior.definition: dē-mōlior ītus, īrī, dep., to throw down, tear down, raze, demolish: hanc (domum): statuas: signum: tyrannidis propugnacula, N.—Fig., to abolish, demolish, destroy: Bacchanalia, L.: aevi prioris Robora, O.: ius, L.

demolitio.definition: dēmōlītiō ōnis, f demolior, a tearing down, demolishing : ea (statuarum): signorum.

demonstratio.definition: dēmōnstrātiō ōnis, f demonstro, a showing, pointing out, description : gestus sententiam demonstratione declarans: conversam habere.— An exposition, explanation : huius generis: quem ad modum quidque fiat.— Demonstrat…

demonstrativus.definition: dēmōnstrātīvus adj. demonstro, designating, demonstrative : genus (orationis), a branch of rhetoric employed in depicting a person .

demonstrator.definition: dēmōnstrātor ōris, m demonstro, one who points out, an indicator, guide : unius cuiusque sepeliendi.

demonstro.definition: dē-mōnstrō āvī, ātus, āre, to point out, indicate, designate, show: figuram digito: ubi habitet (mihi) demonstrarier, T.: itinera: quid ubique esset: finīs, i. e. to deliver possession (of land): demonstrant astra sal…

demorior.definition: (dē-morior) mortuus, ī, to die off, die (out of a number): sacerdotes demortui sunt novique suffecti, L.: ex veterum numero senator: emere in demortui locum: in demortui locum censor sufficitur, L.

demoror.definition: dē-moror ātus, ārī, dep., to retard, detain, delay: vos: hoste iter demorante, Cs.: Teucros armis, restrain from battle, V.: fando Austros, V.: annos, i. e. remain alive, V.: mortalia arma, i. e. await, V.: nihil demo…

demoveo.definition: dē-moveō mōvī, mōtus, ēre, to move away, put away, remove, expel, drive out: demoveri de loco: ex possessione rem p.: hostes gradu demoti, driven back, L.: vestri facti praeiudicio demotus, forced to yield, Cs.—Fig., …

demugitus.definition: dēmūgītus adj. de + mugio, bellowing, resounding with herds : paludes, O.

demulceo.definition: dē-mulceō —, —, ēre, to stroke down, stroke caressingly: tibi caput, T.: dorsum, L.

demum.definition: dēmum adv. de with sup. ending, at length, at last, not till then, just, precisely, only : is demum est iustus triumphus: is demum mihi vivere videtur, qui, etc., no one but him , S.: exsilium quantum demum a perpetuā…

demuneror.definition: dē-mūneror —, ārī, dep., to fee, bribe: ancillas, T.

demurmuro.definition: dē-murmurō —, —, āre, to mutter over: carmen, O.

demutatio.definition: dēmūtātīō ōnis, f demuto, a degeneracy, perversion : morum.

demuto.definition: dē-mūtō āvī, ātus, āre, to change, alter: placitum ‘instituto flaminum nihil demutari,’ Ta.

denarius.definition: dēnārius (gen plur. -iūm; rarely -iōrum), adj. deni, containing ten each ; hence, worth ten (asses): nummus, a silver coin, originally of ten, afterwards of sixteen asses (about 8 d ., $0.16): pendere denarios nummos …

denarro.definition: dē-nārrō —, —, āre, to tell, relate, narrate: Haec illi, T.: matri, ut, etc., H.

denato.definition: dē-natō —, —, āre, to swim down: Tusco alveo, H.

denego.definition: dē-negō āvī, ātus, āre, to reject, refuse, deny: denegandi pudor, T.: conloquia denegata, Cs.: mihi, to say no: quod antea petenti denegasset, Cs.: quod iracundiae denegavisti: honorem homini: operam rei p.: se commis…

deni.definition: dēnī ae, a (gen. dēnūm, C.; dē nōrum, L.), num distrib., ten each, ten at a time, by tens: uxo res habent deni inter se communīs, Cs.: uxores denas habere, S.: pueri annorum septenūm denūm.—Ten (poet. for decem): Bis …

denicalis.definition: dēnicālis e, adj. de + nex, purifying from death : feriae, a service for purification, after a death in the household .

denique.definition: dēnique adv., and thenceforward, and thereafter, at last, at length, finally, lastly, only, not until : denique Metuebant me, T.: Metui, quid futurum denique esset, T.: post biennium denique appellas: octavo denique m…

denomino.definition: dē-nōminō āvī, ātus, āre, to call, name: (ab Lamo) Lamiae denominati, H.

denormo.definition: dē-nōrmō —, —, āre de + norma, to disfigure, make irregular : (angulus) agellum, H.

denoto.definition: dē-notō āvī, ātus, āre, to mark out, point out, specify, indicate, designate: civīs Romanos trucidandos: Icilios denotante senatu, L.—Fig., to take note of, mark, observe closely: denotandis hominum palloribus, Ta.: r…

dens.definition: dēns dentis, m ED-, a tooth : dentibus in ore constructis: eorum adversi acuti ... intimi, qui genuini vocantur, the front teeth ... grinders : puer, nondum omni dente renato, Iu.: dentī s exacuit sus, tusks , V.: vip…

dense.definition: (dēnsē) adv. densus, closely, in quick succession .— Only comp: idem apud alios densius: Nulla subeunt mihi tempora densius istis, O.

denseo.definition: dēnseō —, —, ēre densus, to make thick, thicken, pack, close, press : favilla corpus in unum densetur, O.: Iuppiter Denset erant quae rara, V.: pectine opus, O.: Agmina densentur campis, V.: hastilia, hurl a shower of…

denso.definition: dēnsō —, ātus, āre densus, to make thick, thicken, press, pack, close : catervas, V.: densari ordines iussit, L.: scutis super capita densatis, L.: corpus in unum densatur, O.: obtentā densantur nocte tenebrae, V.: ma…

densus.definition: dēnsus adj. with comp. and sup, thick, close, compact, dense, crowded: silva: densiores silvae, Cs.: densissimae silvae, Cs.: densum umeris volgus, H.: litus, sandy, O.: caligo, V.: densissima nox, pitch-dark, O.: pin…

dentalia.definition: dentālia ium, n dens, the share-beam (of a plough), V.

dentatus.definition: dentātus adj. dens, having teeth : serrula: male, O.— Polished with a tooth : charta.

denubo.definition: dē-nūbō ūpsī, ūptus, ere, to marry away, go away in marriage: in ullos thalamos, O.—To marry beneath one's rank: in domum Blandi.— Cf a mock marriage: in modum solemnium confugiorum, Ta.

denudo.definition: dē-nūdō āvī, ātus, āre, to lay bare, make naked, denude, uncover: denudatis ossibus: ne denudeter a pectore.— Fig., to disclose, reveal, detect, betray, expose: indicia sua, L.: mihi suum consilium, L. —To strip, plun…

denuntiatio.definition: dēnūntiātiō ōnis, f denuntio, an indication, announcement, declaration, proclamation, threat : denuntiationi parere: calamitatum: belli: testimoni, a summons to testify : periculi, a menace , Cs.: terroris, L.: senatū…

denuntio.definition: dē-nūntiō āvī, ātus, āre, to announce, declare, denounce, menace, threaten, intimate, order, command: inimicitias mihi: populo R. servitutem: ab amico timor denuntiari solet?: sese procuratorem esse: eos cavendos esse…

denuo.definition: dēnuō adv. de + novo, once more, a second time, anew, afresh, again : Etruria rebellans, L.: Sicilia censa denuo est: recita denuo: iube mi denuo Respondeat, T.— In turn, again (colloq.): metuo ne denuo Miser excludar…

denus.definition: dēnus adj. for * dec-nus; cf. decem, de/ka, the tenth : luna, O.

deonero.definition: de-onerō āvī, ātus, āre, to unload, disburden: ex illius invidiā aliquid et in te traicere.

deorsum.definition: deorsum or deorsus adv. de+vorsum, vorsus.—Of motion, downwards, down : pondere ferri.—With sursum, up and down : Ne sursum deorsum cursites, T.: naturis sursum deorsum commeantibus.— Of position, down, below : Clivos…

depasco.definition: dē-pāscō pāvī, pāstus, ere, to feed down, feed off, give for food: saltūs, O.: luxuriem segetum, V.—To feed upon, graze, consume: agros: (tauri) summa Lycaei, V.: saepes Hyblaeis apibus florem depasta salicti, V.—Poet…

depascor.definition: dē-pāscor pāstus, ī, dep., to eat up, feed on, consume: morsu artūs, V.: piscis Depastus vivaria, lu.—To waste, destroy: artūs depascitur febris, V.

depecto.definition: dē-pectō —, pexus, ere, to comb off, comb down, comb: crinīs buxo, O.: depexus crinibus, O.: vellera foliis, V.—To comb down, flog, curry (colloq.), T.

depeculator.definition: dēpecūlātor ōris, m depeculor, a plunderer, embezzler : aerari: suus (i. e. eorum).

depeculor.definition: dēpecūlor ātus, ārī cf. peculium, to despoil, plunder, strip : delubra: Apollonium argento.— To embezzle, acquire by fraud : laudem familiae.

depello.definition: dē-pellō pulī, pulsus, ere, to drive out, drive away, remove, expel, put out, put off, turn aside: venientem in forum virum vi: de Falerno Anseres: eum de provinciā, N.: alqm urbe, to banish, Ta.: ab aris et focis fer…

dependeo.definition: dē-pendeō —, —, ēre, to hang from, hang on, hang down: ex umeris nodo dependet amictus, V.: galea ramis, V.: serta tectis, O.: laqueo, L.: Licia dependent, O.—Fig., to be dependent on, wait for: Dependet fides a venie…

dependo.definition: dē-pendō dī, —, ere, to pay: dependendum tibi est, quod mihi spopondisti.—Fig., to pay, render: rei p. poenas.

deperdo.definition: dē-perdō didī, ditus, ere, to destroy, ruin: sutor inopiā deperditus, i. e. impoverished, Ph.: deperditus alquā, desperately in love with, Pr.: in alquā, Ct.: fletu, exhausted, Ct.—To lose: bona, honestatem: tantum ei…

depereo.definition: dē-pereō iī, itūrus, īre, to go to ruin, perish, die, be lost, be undone: tempestate deperierant naves, Cs.: exercitū s magna pars, Cs.: qui deperiit minor uno mense, H.: gens hominum vitio deperitura fuit, O.—To be d…

depingo.definition: dē-pīngō pinxi, pictus, ere, to depict, portray, paint, draw: pugnam, N.—Fig., to portray, represent, describe, imagine, conceive: probe horum facta, T.: vitam huiusce: minuta quaedam nimiumque depicta, too elaboratel…

deplango.definition: dē-plangō nxī, —, ere, to bewail, lament (by beating the breast, etc.): plamis Deplanxere domum, O.: deplangitur Ardea pennis, O.

deploro.definition: de-plōrō āvī, ātus, āre, to weep bitterly, moan, wail, lament, complain: lamentabili voce: de isdem rebus esse dolentius deplorandum.—With acc, to bewail, lament, deplore: ad saxa haec: damnationem illam: domum incens…

depluo.definition: dē-pluō uī, —, ere, to rain down: Multus ut in terras deplueret lapis, Tb.

depono.definition: dē-pōnō posuī (-posīvī, Ct.), positus, ere, to lay away, put aside, set down, lay, place, set, deposit: lecticā paulisper depositā: corpora sub ramis arboris, V.: mentum in gremiis mimarum: onera iumentis, Cs.: deposi…

depopulatio.definition: dēpopulātiō ōnis, f depopulor, a laying waste, marauding, pillaging : agrorum: aedium: ad depopulationem profecti, L.: iter Antoniorum quid habuit nisi depopulationes?

depopulator.definition: dēpopulātor ōris, m depopulor, a marauder, pillager : fori.

depopulor.definition: dē-populor ātus, ārī, dep., to lay waste, ravage, plunder, pillage: Ambiorigis finīs, Cs.: agros, L.: extrema agri Romani, L.: domos, fana: omne mortalium genus (of pestilence), Ta.— P. pass.: depopulatis agris, laid …

deporto.definition: dē-portō āvī, ātus, āre, to carry down, carry off, take away: frumentum in castra, Cs.: ex Siciliā litteras in Verrem: ossa eius ad matrem, N.: partem exercitūs eo, Cs.: omnem exercitum ex Hispaniā, evacuate, L.—To tr…

deposco.definition: dē-pōscō popōscī, —, ere, to demand, require, request earnestly, call for: unum ad id bellum imperatorem deposci: imperatorem Caesarem: sibi navīs, Cs.: pericula, Ta.: sicut semper depoposcimus, Cs.: omnibus pollicita…

depositum.definition: dēpositum ī, n depositus, a deposit, trust, bailment : reddere depositum.—Poet.: arva iussit Fallere depositum, i. e. fail of a harvest , O.

depravatio.definition: dēprāvātiō ōnis, f depravo, a distortion : quaedam (membrorum): oris.—Fig., a perversion, corruption, vitiation : animi: consuetudinum: nostra, perversity .

depravo.definition: dēprāvō —, ātus, āre de + pravus, to distort, disfigure : quaedam contra naturam depravata. — Fig., to pervert, seduce, corrupt, deprave, spoil : nil est Quin male narrando possit depravarier, T.: ut ea quae conrigere…

deprecabundus.definition: dēprecābundus adj. deprecor, earnestly entreating , Ta.

deprecatio.definition: dēprecātiō ōnis, f deprecor, an averting by prayer, appeal, intercession, plea, apology : periculi: quae deprecatio est ei reliqua, qui, etc.: aequitatis, on the ground of : pro illis, Cu.: deprecatione deorum commove…

deprecator.definition: dēprecātor ōris, m deprecor, an averter, intercessor : miseriarum: pro illius periculo.— An advocate, mediator : sui: apud consulem deprecator vobis adero, L.: salutis meae: ut eo deprecatore a Sequanis impetrarent, C…

deprecor.definition: dē-precor ātus, ārī, dep., to avert by prayer, deprecate, plead against, beg to escape, seek to avoid: ullam ab sese calamitatem: a me patriae querimoniam: nullum genus supplici: mortem, Cs.: inimici imperium, S.: sui…

deprehendo.definition: dē-prehendō or dēprēndō (-praendō ) dī, sus, ere, to take away, seize upon, catch, snatch : deprehensus ex itinere Magius, Cs.: comitatūs in ponte, S.: litterae deprehensae, intercepted, L.: navīs, to seize, Cs.: Argo…

deprehensio.definition: dēprehēnsiō ōnis, f deprehendo, a catching, discovery : manifesta veneni.

depressus.definition: dēpressus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of deprimo, sunken, low : domus: convallis, V.: (libra) depressior orbe, Tb.: locus duodecim pedes humi depressus, S.: vox depressissima, Her.

deprimo.definition: dēprimō pressī, pressus, ere de + premo, to press down, weigh down, sink down, depress : terram: ad mentum depresso supercilio: depresso aratro, V.— To sink (in water): partem navium, Cs.: carinam, O.: classis depress…

deproelior.definition: (dē-proelior,) —, ārī, dep. —P. praes., warring violently: ventos aequore Deproeliantīs, H.

depromo.definition: dē-prōmō prōmpsī, prōmptus, ere, to draw out, draw forth, bring out, fetch: pecuniam ex aerario: tela pharetris, V.: venenum sinu, Ta.— Fig., to draw, derive, obtain: e quibus locis argumenta: alqd vel a peritis vel d…

depropero.definition: dē-properō —, —, āre, to hasten, prepare hastily: coronas, H.

depudet.definition: dēpudet uit, ēre, impers, to cease to shame: depuduit, shame has departed, O.

depugis.definition: dēpūgis (depȳgis) is, adj. puga, without buttocks, thin buttocked , H.

depugno.definition: dē-pūgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to fight decisively, fight out, join battle, combat: signis conlatis, L.: acie instructā, Cs.: cum civibus: ad depugnandum, N.: ante depugnabitur: depugnatum cum Gallis est, L.—Fig., to conten…

depulsio.definition: dēpulsiō ōnis, f de+1 PAL-, a driving off, driving away, repelling, warding off : mali: servitutis.— A defence, answer (to a charge), C.— A lowering, sinking : luminum.

depulsor.definition: dēpulsor ōris, m de+1 PAL-, a destroyer : dominatū s.

deputo.definition: dē-putō āvī, ātus, āre, to cut off, prune: umbras (i. e. ramos), O.—To reckon, estimate, esteem, consider: meam esse operam parvi preti, T.: malo se dignum deputat.

derecte.definition: dērēctē adv. with comp. derectus, directly, straight : dicere: derectius gubernare.

derecto.definition: dērēctō adv. derectus, directly, straight : trabī s inicere, Cs.: deorsus ferri.—Fig., simply, directly, unambiguously : dicere: arma petisse, L.

derectus.definition: dērēctus (dīrēctus) adj. P. of derigo, straight, direct, level, upright, perpendicular : (iter) simplex et derectum: tuba derecti (aeris), O.: fossam derectis lateribus ducere, Cs.: iugum eminens in mare, Cs.: Henna a…

derelictio.definition: dērelictiō ōnis, f derelinquo, an abandoning, disregard, neglect : communis utilitatis.

derelictus.definition: dērelictus adj. P. of derelinquo, solitary, deserted : angulus provinciae: solum.

derelinquo.definition: dē-relinquō līquī, lictus, ere, to forsake wholly, abandon, desert: Gracchum a Tuberone derelictum videbamus: arationes: ab omni fortunā derelicti: filium privatum dereliquerat, S.: oppida pro derelicto habere, abando…

derepente.definition: dē-repentē adv., suddenly, on a sudden: ab eā sese avellere, T.: rabere, C. poët.

derepo.definition: dē-rēpō rēpsī, —, ere, to crawl down, sneak down: ad cubile suis, Ph.

derideo.definition: dē-rīdeō sī, sus, ēre, to laugh at, laugh to scorn, scoff at, deride, mock: omnīs istos: te, H.: derisum esse credo hominem: alqd, H.: derisus semel, hooted off: derideat Aethiopem albus, In.: merito, T.: deridet, cum…

deridiculus.definition: dē-rīdīculus adj., very laughable, ridiculous: deridiculum esse se reddere, etc., L. dub.—As subst n., an object of ridicule, laughing stock, mockery: deridiculo esse, Ta.: per deridiculum auditur, Ta.: corporis, ludi…

derigesco.definition: (dē-rigēscō) dēriguī, or dīriguī , —, ere, inch, to become stiff, grow rigid, fix, curdle (only perf. system): formidine sanguis deriguit, V.: deriguere oculi, were fixed, V.: hirsutae comae, O.

derigo.definition: dērigō or dēregō or dīrigō rēxī, rēctus, ere de + rego, to lay straight, set straight, arrange, lay out : haec directä materiā iniecta consternebantur, Cs.: cratīs, Cs.: derexerat finem Philippo veterem viam regiam, L…

deripio.definition: dēripiō ripuī, reptus, ere de + rapio, to tear off, tear away, snatch away, remove violently, pull down : cothurnos, V.: de manu Cereris Victoriam: vestem a pectore, O.: velamina ex umeris, O.: ei vitae ornamenta deri…

derisor.definition: dērīsor ōris, m derideo, a mocker, scoffer : semper eris, H.: populi, Iu.: imi lecti, H.

derisus2.definition: dērīsus ūs, m derideo, mockery, scorn, derision : facile ad derisum stulta levitas ducitur, Ph.: derisui fuisse triumphum, Ta.

derivatio.definition: dērīvātiō ōnis, f derivo, a leading off, turning away : (lacūs). L.—Plur: fluminum.

derivo.definition: dērīvō āvī, ātus, āre de + rivus, to lead off, turn away : aqua ex flumine derivata, Cs.—Fig., to draw, derive, bring : nihil in suam domum inde: Hoc fonte derivata clades, H.— To divert, turn aside, transfer : in me …

derogatio.definition: dērogātiō ōnis, f derogo, a partial abrogation, limitation (of a law).
