derosus.definition: dē-rōsus P., gnawed away, nibbled: clipei a muribus.

deruo.definition: dē-ruō ruī, —, ere, to take away, detract: cumulum de laudibus alicuius.

deruptus.definition: dē-ruptus adj. with comp, broken, precipitous, steep: angustiae, L.: in deruptiorem tumulum, L. — Plur n. as subst, precipices, L.

desaevio.definition: dē-saeviō iī, —, īre, to rave furiously, rage: in aequore, V.: pelago hiems, V.: tragicā in arte, H.

descendo.definition: dē-scendō dī, sus, ere, to climb down, come down, descend, fall, sink: ex equo, to alight: monte, S.: de palatio: caelo, H.: e caelo, Iu.: vertice montis ab alto, V.: ab Alpibus, L.: arce Monoeci, V.: per clivum, O.: …

descensio.definition: dēscēnsiō ōnis, f descendo, a descending : Tiberina, the sail down the Tiber .

descensus.definition: dēscēnsus ūs, m descendo, a descent, way down : quā illi descensus erat, S.: facilis descensus Averno, V.: difficilis et artae viae, L.

descisco.definition: dē-scīscō īvī, ītus, ere, to withdraw, leave, revolt from, desert, go over: ab Afranio, Cs.: a populo: quibus invitis descitum ad Samnites erat, L.: aperte, L.— In gen., to depart, deviate, withdraw, fall off, be unfa…

describo.definition: dē-scrībō īpsī, īptus, ere (often confounded with discribo), to copy off, transcribe, write out, write down: a te librum (i. e. a tuo exemplo): descriptam legem adferunt, the draf<*> in foliis carmina, V.: in cortice …

descripte.definition: dēscrīptē adv. descriptus, in an orderly manner : digerere.

descriptio.definition: dēscrīptiō ōnis (often confounded with discriptio), f describo, a marking out, delineation, copy, transcript, draft : caeli, circuit : tabularum: alqd descriptionibus explicare.—Fig., a representation, delineation, de…

descriptus.definition: dēscrīptus adj. with comp. P. of describo, precisely ordered, properly arranged : materies orationis: ordo verborum: naturā nihil est descriptius.

deseco.definition: dē-secō cuī, ctus, āre, to cut off, cut away: aurīs, Cs.: cervice desectā, L.: particulam undique, H.: hordeum, Cs.: desecta cum stramento seges, L.: Desectum gramen, O.—Fig., to prune off, reject: illud (prooemium).

desero.definition: dē-serō ruī, rtus, ere, to leave, forsake, abandon, desert, give up: exercitum, Cs.: castra, L.: castellis desertis, Cs.: fratrem, V.: thalamos pactos, V.: Mensa deserit toros, is removed from, O.: Raro scelestum Dese…

desertor.definition: dēsertor ōris, m desero, one who forsakes, a deserter : amicorum: communis utilitatis aut salutis.—In war, a runaway, deserter , Cs., L., Ta.— Poet.: Amoris, O.: Asiae, V.

desertus.definition: dēsertus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of desero, deserted, desert, solitary, lonely, waste : angiportus, T.: anus, T.: planities penuriā aquae, S.: loca, Cs.: urbes: via: portūs, V.: vetustas, long disuse , H.: reditus…

deservio.definition: dē-serviō —, —, īre, to serve zealously, be devoted, be subject, be of service: cuivis deserviant: vobis operā deservire: si officia, si operae, si vigiliae deserviunt amicis: divinis rebus.

deses.definition: (dēses) idis, adj. de + SED-, inactive, indolent, idle : sedemus desides domi mulierum ritu, L.: longā pace desides, Ta.—Fig.: nec rem Romanam tam desidem umquam fuisse, L.

desideo.definition: dēsideō sēdī, —, ēre de + sedeo, to sit long, sit idle, remain inactive : totum diem, T.: aquila ramis, Ph.

desiderabilis.definition: dēsīderābilis e, adj. desidero, wanted, desirable : nihil desiderabile concupiscunt: suis vitiis desiderabilem efficere avum, i. e. missed , L.: princeps, Ta.

desideratio.definition: dēsīderātiō ōnis, f desidero, a desiring, longing, missing : (voluptatum) dub

desiderium.definition: dēsīderium ī, n cf. desidero, a longing, ardent desire, wish, want, grief, regret : Athenarum, T.: urbis, homesickness : coniunctissimi viri: tam cari capitis, H.: pectora diu tenet desiderium, Enn. ap. C.: Ita magno …

desidero.definition: dēsīderō āvī, ātus, āre cf. considero, to long for, ask, demand, call for, wish for, desire, require, expect : me, T.: tribuni imperium, Cs.: ea (beneficia), S.: quod satis est, H.: ullam rem ad se inportari, Cs.: alq…

desidia.definition: dēsidia ae, f deses, a sitting idle, idleness, inactivity, sloth : ab industriā ad desidiam avocari: pro labore desidia, S.: latrocinia desidiae minuendae causā fieri, Cs.: improba Siren, H.: invisa primo desidia post…

desidiosus.definition: dēsidiōsus adj. with sup. desidia, slothful, indolent, lazy, idle : Qui nolet fieri desidiosus, amet, O.— Causing idleness, making lazy : inlecebrae cupiditatum: desidiosissimum otium.

desido.definition: dē-sīdō sīdī, —, ere.—Of places, to sink, settle down, fall: ut multis locis terrae desiderint: ad Manīs imos, V.—Fig., to deteriorate: desidentes mores, L.

designatio.definition: dēsīgnātiō ōnis, f designo, a marking out, specification (cf. dissignatio): personarum et temporum.— A designation to office : annua, of consuls , Ta.

designo.definition: dē-sīgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to mark out, point out, trace, designate, define (often confounded with dissigno): urbem aratro, V.: moenia fossā, V.: templo Iovis finīs, L.: circo designatus locus est, L.: Europen, depicts …

desilio.definition: dēsiliō iluī, ultus, īre de + salio, to leap down, dismount : de navibus, Cs.: de raedā: ex equis, Cs.: ab equo, V.: curru ab alto, O.: biiugis, V.: altis turribus, H.: in medias undas, O.: ad pedes, to dismount , Cs.…

desino.definition: dē-sinō siī (rare; dēstitī is used instead), situs, ere, to leave off, give over, cease, desist, forbear: lacessere, T.: de compositione loqui, Cs.: furere: iudicia severa Romae fieri desierunt: ut auctor Desinat inqu…

desipiens.definition: dēsipiēns entis, adj. P. of desipio, foolish, silly : adrogentia: ita desipiens, qui, etc.

desipio.definition: dēsipiō —, —, ere de + sapio, to be void of understanding, be silly, act foolishly : licet me desipere dicatis: si non desipit augur, H.: Dulce est desipere in loco, to trifle , H.

desisto.definition: dē-sistō stitī, stitus, ere, to leave off, cease, give over, desist from: de quā (petitione) ne aliquid iurares destitisti: de petitione, L.: a defensione, Cs.: ab oppugnatione, S.: litibus, T.: hoc conatu, Cs.: susce…

desolo.definition: dē-sōlō āvī, ātus, āre, to leave alone, forsake, abandon, desert: agros, V.: desolatae terrae, O.: desolatus servilibus ministeriis, deprived of, Ta.

despecto.definition: dēspectō —, —, āre, intens. despicio, to look down upon : terras, V., O.: Palantīs homines procul, O.— To overlook, command : quos despectant moenia, V.— To despise : liberos, Ta.

despectus1.definition: dēspectus adj. with sup. P. of despicio, contemptible, scorned : maxime natura eius, Ta.: despectissima pars servientium, Ta.

despectus2.definition: dēspectus ūs, m despicio, a looking down upon, view, prospect : ex oppido in campum, Cs.: ex omnibus partibus despectū s habere, points of view , Cs.— An object of contempt : ut (res R.) Treveris despectui sit, Ta.

desperanter.definition: dēspēranter adv. despero, hopelessly, despairingly : loqui secum.

desperatio.definition: dēspērātiō ōnis, f despero, hopelessness, despair : summa, Cs.: ad desperationem adducti, N.: a desperatione iram accendit, L.: desperationes eorum, qui, etc.: vitae: nimis celer rerum, L.: magna pacis, Cs.

desperatus.definition: dēspērātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of despero, given up, despaired of, irremediable, desperate : res p.: desperatas pecunias exigere: fuga.—Prov.: desperatis adhibere medicinam: haec nunc multo desperatiora: despe…

despero.definition: dē-spērō āvī, ātus, āre, to be hopeless, have no hope, despair of, give up: de se: de pugnā , Cs.: de toto ordine: de summā rerum, L.: honores: rem p.: vitam: voluntariam deditionem, L.: sive restituimur, sive despera…

despicatio.definition: dēspicātiō ōnis, f 1 despicatus, contempt .— Only plur, sentiments of contempt .

despicatus1.definition: dēspicātus adj. with sup. de+SPEC-, in contempt, despised : nos nostramque adulescentiam Habent despicatam, T.— Contemptible, despicable : despicatissimus homo.

despicatus2.definition: (dēspicātus ūs), m de+SPEC-, contempt .— Only dat: despicatui duci, to be despised .

despiciendus.definition: dēspiciendus adj. P. of despicio, contemptible , Ta.

despiciens.definition: dēspiciēns entis, adj. P. of despicio, contemptuous : tam sui, of so little self-esteem .

despicientia.definition: dēspicientia ae, f despiciens, a despising, contempt : rerum humanarum: animi.

despicio.definition: dēspiciō ēxī, ectus, ere de + specio, to look down upon : de vertice montis in vallīs, O.: colles, quā despici poterat, in the range of view , Cs.— With acc , (some read dispicio in these passages): gentīs et urbīs: a…

despolio.definition: de-spoliō āvī, ātus, āre, to rob, plunder, despoil: se armis, Cs.: ut cum Siculis despoliaretur: despoliari triumpho, L.

despondeo.definition: dē-spondeō spondī, spōnsus, ēre, to promise to give, promise, pledge: librum alicui: Romanis imperium Orientis, L.— To promise in marriage, betroth, engage: ei filiam suam: virgo desponsa uni ex Curiatiis, L.: tibi Ia…

despumo.definition: dē-spūmō —, —, āre, to skim off, skim: foliis undam aëni, V.

despuo.definition: dē-spuō —, —, ere, to spit out, spit upon: ubi despui religio est, L.: in molles sibi sinūs, Tb.— To reject, abhor: preces, Ct.

destillo.definition: dē-stīllō or dī-stīllō —, —, āre, to drip, trickle down: destillat ab inguine virus, V.: Illius puro destillent tempora Nardo, Tb.

destinatio.definition: dēstinātiō ōnis, f destino, an assignment : partium, L.— A resolve, determination : haud dubia, Ta.: destinationis certus, resolute , Ta.

destinatum.definition: dēstinātum ī, n destinatus, a mark, target , L., Cu.—Fig., a plan, purpose : copias ad destinatum eduxit, L.: tuis destinatis adversari, Ta.: destinata dare, the dispositions (of a will), Ph.

destinatus.definition: dēstinātus adj. P. of destino, fixed, determined, destined, inevitable : sententiae: hora mortis: Orci finis, H.: destinatus obdura, resolutely , Ct.

destino.definition: dēstinō āvī, ātus, āre STA-, to make fast, make firm, bind, fix, stay : antemnas ad malos, Cs.: rates ancoris, Cs.—Fig., to fix in mind, determine, resolve, design, assign, devote, appoint, appropriate : eum ducem, fi…

destituo.definition: dēstituō uī, ūtus, ere de + statuo, to set down, set forth, put away, bring forward, leave alone : alios in convivio (in mockery): ante tribunal regis destitutus, L.: ante pedes destitutum causam dicere, L.— To leave,…

destitutio.definition: dēstitūtiō ōnis, f destituo, an abandonment, desertion, disappointment : destitutione irati.

destrictus.definition: dēstrictus adj. P. of destringo, severe, rigid . — Only comp: destrictior accusator, Ta.

destringo.definition: dē-stringo inxī, ictus, ere, to strip off: tunica ab umeris destricta est, Ph.—To unsheathe, draw: gladios in rem p.: gladiis destrictis impetum facere, Cs.: ensem, H.: in se destrictis securis, brandished, L.—To touc…

destruo.definition: dē-struō ūxī, ūctus, ere, to tear down, raze, demolish: navem: moenia, V.—Fig., to destroy, ruin, weaken: id (ius), L.: senem, O.: hostem, Ta.

desubito.definition: dē-subitō or dē subitō adv., on a sudden, suddenly: bolus ereptus e faucibus, T.: funus ornatum.

desudo.definition: dē-sūdō —, —, āre, to sweat, make great exertion: in his (sc. exercitationibus ingeni).

desuefactus.definition: dēsuēfactus adj. desuetus + factus, estranged : multitudo a contionibus.

desuetudo.definition: dēsuētūdō nis, f desuetus, disuse, want of practice : armorum, L.: desuetudine tardi, O.

desuetus.definition: dē-suētus adj., disused, laid aside, unfamiliar, out of use, obsolete: arma diu, V: res, L.: desueta sidera cerno, O.: verba, O.—Out of practice, unaccustomed, unused: triumphis Agmina, V.: corda (amori), V.: Samnis c…

desultor.definition: dēsultor ōris, m de + 2 SAL-, a vaulter, circus-rider : desultorum in modum, L.—Fig.: amoris, i. e. inconstant , O.

desultorius.definition: dēsultōrius adj. desultor, of a vaulter : quasi desultorius, like a circus-rider's horse .

desum.definition: dē-sum fuī, esse (in poetry dee- is one syll.; perf. dēfuērunt, trisyl., O.; fut. inf. dēfutūrum esse or dēfore), to be away, be absent, fail, be wanting, be missing: quasi desit locus, T.: Non ratio, verum argentum d…

desumo.definition: dē-sūmō ūmpsī, —, ere, to take, choose, select: tibi hostīs, L.: sibi vacuas Athenas, H.—To assume, undertake: sibi consules adservandos, L.

desuper.definition: dē-super adv. —Of motion, from above, from overhead: (alqm) volnerare, Cs.: nemus imminet, V.—Of rest, above (poet.): imposuere togas, O.

desurgo.definition: dē-surgō —, —, ere, to rise: cenā, H.

detego.definition: dē-tegō ēxī, ēctus, ere, to uncover, expose, lay bare, unroof: aedem, L.: Caci detecta regia, V.: iuga montium detexerat nebula, L.: caput puer detectus, with bare head, V.: ossa, O.: detecta corpora: arcana profanā m…

detendo.definition: dē-tendō —, sus, ere, to unstretch: tabernaculis detensis, struck, Cs.: tabernacula, L.

detergeo.definition: dē-tergeō (plur. once detergunt, L.), sī, sus, ere, to wipe off, wipe away: lacrimas pollice, O.: nubila caelo, i. e. to clear, H.—To wipe, cleanse: volnera mappā , Iu.: cloacas, L.—To strip off, break off: remos, Cs.…

deterior.definition: dēterior ius, adj. comp. with sup. dēterrimus de, lower, worse, poorer, meaner : tempus, less favorable : status: vectigalia sibi deteriora facere, Cs.: muraena carne, H.: aetas, V.: quo (peditatu) erat deteriore, i. …

deterius.definition: dēterius adv. deterior, worse, less : scripta: interpretari, unfavorably , Ta.: si placeant spe Deterius, H.: nilo deterius, nevertheless , H.

determinatio.definition: dēterminātiō ōnis, f determino, a boundary, conclusion : mundi: orationis.

determino.definition: dē-terminō āvī, ātus, āre, to enclose, bound, limit, prescribe: regiones ab oriente ad occasum, L.—To fix, settle, determine: spiritu, non arte, ends (his sentences): Omnia determinat annus, C. poët.

detero.definition: dē-terō trīvī, trītus, ere, to rub away, wear away: detritae aequore conchae, O.: pedes (via), Tb.: a catenā collum detritum, Ph.—Fig., to lessen, weaken, impair: laudes Caesaris culpā ingeni, H.: Exiguis (rebus) aliq…

deterreo.definition: dē-terreō uī, itus, ēre, to frighten off, deter, discourage, prevent, hinder: reliquos magnitudine poenae, Cs.: testīs verbis: pavidam ense, O.: deterritis tribunis, L.: in deterrendā liberalitate. adulescentīs a dice…

detestabilis.definition: dētestābilis e, adj. with comp. detestor, execrable, abominable, detestable : omen: nihil esse tam detestabile quam voluptatem: exemplum, L.: detestabilior immanitas.

detestandus.definition: detestandus adj. P. of detestor, execrable : fraus, Ta.

detestatio.definition: dētestātiō ōnis, f detestor, the invocation of a curse : eā detestatione obstricti, L.: dira, H. — An averting by sacrifice, deprecation : scelerum.

detestatus.definition: dētestātus adj. P. of detestor, accursed, hateful, abominable : detestata omnia eius modi repudianda sunt: bella matribus Detestata, H.

detestor.definition: dē-testor ātus, ārī, dep., to curse, execrate, abominate: (te) tamquam auspicium malum: omnibus precibus Ambiorigem, Cs.: caput euntis hostili prece, O.: carmen detestandae familiae compositum, for an imprecation on t…

detexo.definition: dē-texō —, xtus, ere, to weave, plait: aliquid Viminibus, V.: fiscellam vimine, Tb.—Fig.: detexta prope retexantur, finished.

detineo.definition: dētineō tinuī, tentus, ēre de + teneo, to hold off, keep back, detain, check : a quo incepto me ambitio detinuerat, S.: me detinuit morbus, T.: civium numerum tam bonis rebus: contionibus detinenda plebs, L.: me his o…

detondeo.definition: dē-tondeō —, tōnsus, ēre, to shear off, cut off, clip, shear: crinīs, O.: detonsae frigore frondes, i. e. stripped off, O.

detono.definition: dē-tonō uī, —, āre, to thunder down, thunder: (Iuppiter) ubi detonuit, O.—To have done thundering: nubem belli, dum detonet omnis, Sustinet, exhaust its rage, V.

detorqueo.definition: dē-torqueō sī, tus, ēre, to bend aside, turn off, turn away, turn, direct: ponticulum: Ora dextrā equorum, V.: lumen ab illā, O.: volnus, averted, V.: alqd in dextram partem: ad regem cursūs, V.: cervicem ad oscula, H…

detractio.definition: dētrāctiō ōnis, f detraho, a taking away, wresting, withdrawal, removal : (Praxitelia capita) efficiuntur detractione, cutting away : alieni: cibi, a purging .

detractor.definition: dētrāctor ōris, m de + TRAG-, a disparager : sui, Ta.

detraho.definition: dē-trahō trāxī, trāctus, ere, to draw off, take down, pull down, take away, remove, withdraw, drag, bring: soccos detrahunt (servi), T.: detractis insignibus imperatoris, Cs.: vestem: pellem, H.: alquem in iudicium: d…

detrectatio.definition: dētrectātiō (dētrāct-) ōnis, f detrecto, a declining, refusing : militiae, L.: sine detrectatione, L.

detrectator.definition: dētrectātor (detrāct-) ōris, m detrecto, a diminisher, disparager : laudum suarum, L.

detrecto.definition: dētrectō or dē-trāctō avī , ātus, āre, to decline, refuse, reject, shirk: militiam, Cs.: pericula, Ta.: certamen, L.: iuga, V.: vincla pedum, Tb.: alcuius iussa, Ta.: num consulto detrectarent, L. —Fig., to lower in e…

detrimentosus.definition: dētrīmentōsus adj. detrimentum, hurtful, detrimental : discedere detrimentosum esse, Cs.

detrimentum.definition: dētrīmentum ī, n de + 1 TER-, that which is worn away : ergastuli detrimenta (of men), wrecks of the work-house , Cu.— Wear and tear, loss, damage, detriment : exercitūs, Cs.: militum, Cs.: existimationis, N.: de te f…

detrudo.definition: dē-trūdō sī, sus, ere, to thrust away, thrust down, push down, push off, strip off: in pistrinum: in solidam acumina (pedum) erram, O.: caput sub Tartara telo, V.: sub inania Tartara, O.: navīs scopulo, V.: scutis teg…

detrunco.definition: dē-truncō āvī, ātus, āre, to lop, cut off: arbores, L.: caput, O.—To mutilate, maim, behead: gladio detruncata corpora, L.

deturbo.definition: dē-turbō āvī, ātus, āre, to thrust down, beat down, expel, overthrow, tear down, hurl, strike down: ex turribus propugnantīs, Cs.: ex praesidiis Macedonas, L.: lapidibus coniectis deturbati, dislodged, Cs.: nitentīs p…

deunx.definition: de-ūnx ūncis, m de + uncia, eleven twelfths : habet Gillo deuncem, Iu.: heres ex deunce.

deuro.definition: de-ūrō ūssī, ūstus, ere, to burn up, consume, destroy: deusti plutei turrium, Cs.: vicum, L.—Of frost: hiems arbores deusserat, L.

deus.definition: deus ī (nom plur. dī, diī, rarely deī ; gen. deōrum or deūm, poet. also divōm or divū m; dat. dīs, diīs, and later deīs), m DIV-, a god, deity : deorum inmortalium numen: consilio deorum, Cs.— In ejaculations: di! T.:…

deutor.definition: de-ūtor —, ūtī, dep., to maltreat: victo, N.

devasto.definition: dē-vāstō —, ātus, āre, to lay waste, devastate: finīs, L.: Marsos, L.: agmina ferro devastata, O.

deveho.definition: de-vehō vexī, vectus, ere, to carry down, carry off, convey, take away: (carinas) carris iunctis milia passuum a castris XXII, Cs.: legionem equis, Cs.: maximos commeatūs Tiberis devexit, L.: devecta cremato sarmenta,…

develo.definition: dē-vēlō —, —, āre, to unveil, uncover: Ora sororis, O.

deveneror.definition: dē-veneror ātus, ārī, dep., to reverence, worship: deos prece, O.—To avert by prayer: somnia, Tb.

devenio.definition: dē-veniō vēnī, ventūrus, īre, to come, arrive, reach: alquam in partem, Cs.: ad eam necessario: in victoris manūs: in eum locum, L.: in Scythiam, O.: quo, H.—With acc: devenere locos ubi, etc., V.: speluncam eandem, V…

deverbero.definition: dē-verberō āvī, —, āre, to thrash, cudgel soundly: homines usque ad necem, T.

deversor.definition: dē-versor (-vorsor) ātus, ārī, dep., to tarry, put up, lodge as a guest: Athenis apud eum: apud Ninnios, L.: hac in domo tam diu: domi suae: parum laute.

deversoriolum.definition: dēversōriolum ī, n dim. deversorium, a small lodging-place .

deversorium.definition: dēversōrium (dēvors-, dīvers-) ī, n deversor, an inn, lodging-house : commorandi: hospitale, L.: flagitiorum omnium: nota, H.

deverticulum.definition: dēverticulum (dīvert-, dēvort-) ī, n deverto, a by-road, by-path, side-way : quae deverticula quaesivisti?: Ubi ad ipsum veni devorticulum, T.— An inn, lodging-house, tavern : omnia loca deverticuli protraherentur, L.…

deverto.definition: dē-vertō or dēvortō tī, —, ere, to turn away, turn aside, turn in, put up, betake oneself, go to lodge: viā devertit, loses the way, L.: ad coponem: eius domum: in villam Pompei.—Fig., to digress: redeamus illuc, unde…

devertor.definition: dēvertor or dēvortor sus, tī, dep. collat. form of deverto, to turn away, turn aside, turn in, put up, go to lodge : itineris causā: locus quo deverteretur: quā nulla Castaliam molli devertitur orbita clivo, V.: apud …

devexus.definition: dēvexus adj. deveho, inclining, sloping, shelving, steep : lucus a Palati radice in novam viam: mundus in Austros, V.: amnis, V.: haec declivia et devexa, Cs.: arva, O.: Orion, i. e. towards his setting , H.: raeda, o…

devincio.definition: dē-vinciō nxī, nctus, ere, to bind fast, tie up, fetter, clamp: aliquem fasciis: operculis plumbo devinctis, L.—Fig., to bind fast, unite closely, oblige, lay under obligation: (Italiam) omnibus vinclis devinctam tene…

devinco.definition: dē-vincō vīcī, vīctus, ere, to conquer completely, overcome, subdue: Galliam, Cs.: Capuam: Poenos classe: devicti reges, H.: devicta Asia, V.: devicto (mihi) restabat, O.: devicta bella, victoriously concluded, V.—Fig…

devinctus.definition: dē-vinctus adj. with comp. P. of devincio, devoted, strongly attached : studiis a pueritiā: alcui me devinctior, H.

devitatio.definition: dēvītātiō ōnis, f devito, an avoiding : legionum.

devito.definition: dē-vītō āvī, ātus, āre, to avoid, shun: procellam temporis: Quae (mala), T.: repulsam, H.

devius.definition: dēvius adj. de + via, off the road, out of the way, devious : iter, a by-way : oppidum: calles, L.: rura, O.— Retired, sequestered : Anagnini: gens, L.: mihi devio libet, etc., wandering in byways , H.: avis, i. e. th…

devoco.definition: dē-vocō āvī, ātus, āre, to call off, call away, recall: eum de provinciā: ab tumulo suos, L.: ex praesidiis, L.: refixa sidera caelo, H.: Iovem ad auxilium, L.—Fig., to call off, allure, bring down: philosophiam e cae…

devolo.definition: dē-volō —, ātūrus, āre, to fly down: Iris per caelum, V.: sibi de caelo devolatura in sinum victoria, L.—To fly away: turdus devolet illuc, ubi, etc., H.—To hasten down, hasten away, fly: praecipites pavore in forum, …

devolvo.definition: dē-volvō volvī, volūtus, ere, to roll down: saxa in musculum, Cs.: Auratas trabes, V.: tonitrua (i. e. balls to make scenic thunder), Ph.: corpora in humum, O.: magnos corpore montīs, O.: fusis mollia pensa, i. e. to …

devoro.definition: dē-vorō āvī, ātus, āre, to swallow, gulp down, devour, consume: id quod devoratur: Pro epulis auras, O.—To swallow up, ingulf, absorb: devorer telluris hiatu, O.: vel me Charybdis devoret, O.— To seize greedily, swall…

devortium.definition: dēvortium ī deverto, a by-way : devortia itinerum, Ta. (al. div-).

devotio.definition: dēvōtiō ōnis, f devoveo, a self-sacrifice, offering : eius devotionis convictus: vitae: capitis.— A cursing, execration, outlawry : eius devotionis memoria, N.: in quibus (pilis) scripta, N.— A formula of execration ,…

devotus.definition: dēvōtus adj. P. of devoveo, bowed, devoted, accursed : arbos, H.: periuria, Ct.— Devoted, attached, faithful : tibi cliens, Iu.— As subst: cum DC devotis, faithful followers , Cs.—Fig., given, abandoned : vino, Ph.

devoveo.definition: dē-voveō vōvī, vōtus, ēre, to vow, devote, offer, sacrifice: Marti ea, quae bello ceperint, Cs.: Dianae alqd pulcherrimum: gnatam pro mutā agnā, H.: se ipsos dis pro re p.: se pro patriā, L.: se aris, V.: auspicio se:…

dextella.definition: dextella ae, f dim. dextra, a little right hand : Q. filius illius est dextella.

dexter.definition: dexter tera, terum, and tra, trum, adj. with comp. dexterior and sup. dextimus, to the right, on the right side, right (opp. laevus, sinister): manus: umeri, Cs.: latus, H.: hostium, Cs.: cornum, T.: cornu, Cs.: acies…

dextera.definition: dextera or dextra ae, f dexter, sc. manus, the right hand : Cedo dextram, T.: eius dextram, prendit, Cs.: per dexteram te istam oro: dexterae, quae fidei testes esse solebant: fidem dextrā dare, N.: si Pergama dextrā …

dextere.definition: dexterē and dextrē adv. with comp. dexter, dexterously, skilfully : obeundo officia, L.: nemo dexterius fortunā est usus, played his cards better , H.

dexteritas.definition: dexteritās ātis, f dexter, dexterity, aptness : ad omnia ingeni dexteritas, L.

dextra.definition: dextrā praep. abl. of dextera, on the right of : dextrā viam stratam, L.

dextrorsum.definition: dextrōrsum or dextrōrsus adv. dexter + vorsus, towards the right side, to the right : dextrorsum abire, H.: dextrorsus pergere, L.

diadema.definition: diadēma ātis, n , dia/dhma, a royal headdress, diadem: conlegae diadema imponere: tutum, H.

diaeta.definition: diaeta ae, f , di/aita, a regular mode of living, diet: diaetā curari.

dialectica1.definition: dialectica ae, f sc. ars, dialectics, logic .

dialectica2.definition: dialectica ōrum, n dialecticus, logical discussion, dialectics .

dialectice.definition: dialecticē adv. dialecticus, logically, dialectically : disputare: dicta multa.

dialecticus.definition: dialecticus adj. , dialektiko/s, belonging to disputation, dialectic: captiones.—As subst m., a dialectician, logician.

dialogus.definition: dialogus ī, m , dia/logos, a discussion, treatise in conversational form, dialogue.

diarium.definition: (diārium ī), n dies, a daily ration (only plur.): diariis militum celeritatem incitat: cum servis diaria rodere, H.

dibaphus.definition: dibaphus ī, f , di/bafos (prop. double dyed), a purple robe, magistrate's state-robe.

dica.definition: dica ae, f , di/kh, a lawsuit, judicial process, action: omnibus dicis diem distulit, adjourned all actions.—In the phrases: dicam scribere, to bring an action: tibi scribam dicam, against thee, T.: iniuriarum mihi sc…

dicacitas.definition: dicācitās ātis, f dicax, biting wit, raillery .

dicatio.definition: dicātiō ōnis, f 1 dico, a formal declaration (in changing one's citizenship).

dicax.definition: dicāx ācis, adj. with comp. DIC-, talking sharply, satirical, sarcastic, acute, witty : Demosthenes: Satyri, wanton , H.: dicacior naturā , L.

dichoreus.definition: dichorēus ī, m , dixo/reios, a double trochee.

dicio.definition: (diciō) ōnis, f DIC-, dominion, sovereignty, authority, sway, control, rule (only sing; no nom.): oram Romanae dicionis fecit, brought under , L.: regna virūm dicioni permissa: civitates in dicionem populi R. redactas…

dicis.definition: dicis gen. DIC-.—Only in the phrase dicis causā , for form's sake, for the sake of appearance : illis aliquid dicis causā dare: quae (provinciae) iis dicis causā datae erant, N.

dico1.definition: dicō āvī, ātus, āre * dicus; DIC-, to dedicate, consecrate, devote : donum (Iovi) dicatum: ara condita atque dicata, L.: tibi aram dicatum iri, L.: templum Iovis, O., L.: templa sibi (patri), V.: vehiculum, Ta.— To gi…

dico2.definition: dīcō dīxī, dictus (imper. dī c; perf. often <*>ync. dīxtī; P. praes. gen. plur. dī centum for dīcentium, O.), ere DIC-, to say, speak, utter, tell, mention, relate, affirm, declare, state, assert : ille, quem dixi, me…

dicrotum.definition: dicrotum ī, n , =di/kroton, a galley with two banks of oars.

dictamnus.definition: dictamnus ī, f , =di/ktamnos, dittany (an herb), C., V.

dictata.definition: dictāta ōrum, n things dictated, lessons, exercises: orationem tamquam dictata perdiscere: haec, H.—Precepts, rules, Iu.

dictator.definition: dictātor ōris, m dicto.—In Rome, a dictator, chief magistrate with unlimited power (in great emergencies, superseding ordinary magistracies): lex de dictatore lata, Cs.: nomen dictatoris sustulisti: creandi dictatoris…

dictatorius.definition: dictātōrius adj. dictator, of a dictator, dictatorial : stilus: maiestas, L.: iuvenis, i. e. the son of the dictator , L.

dictatura.definition: dictātūra ae, f dictator, the office of a dictator, dictatorship : perpetua: dictaturā se abdicat, Cs.: abdicata, inita, L.

dictio.definition: dictiō ōnis, f DIC-, a saying, speaking, uttering, delivery : testimoni, i. e. the right of giving testimony , T.: causae, a pleading .—Esp., in the phrase, iuris dictio, the administration of justice : ut iuris dicti…

dictito.definition: dictitō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. dicto, to say often, declare, maintain, assert, insist : non es Quem semper te esse dictitasti? T.: qui ita dictitat, iis esse metuendum, etc.: si te populus sanum dictitet, H.— To plea…

dicto.definition: dīctō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. 2 dico, to dictate, suggest, remind : tu idem, qui illis orationem dictavisses, put in their mouths : Mercemur servum qui dictet nomina (i. e. nomenclatorem), H.: Tironi (opp. ipse scribere…

dictum.definition: dictum ī, n DIC-, something said, a saying, word, assertion, remark : mihi Scripta illa dicta sunt in animo, T.: quod dictum graviter ferebant, Cs.: Metelli dicta cum factis conposuit, S.: ferocia, L.: inurbanum, H.: …

dido.definition: dī-dō dīdidī, dīditus, ere, to give out, spread abroad, disseminate, distribute, scatter (poet.): dide ac dissice, Caecil. ap. C.: dum munia didit (sc. servis), H.: Diditur per agmina rumor, V.: tua terris didita fama…

diduco.definition: dī-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to draw apart, part, split, separate, sever, sunder, divide, undo, relax: digitos: risu rictum Auditoris, H.: nodos manu, O.: arva et urbīs, V.: fores, Ta.: scopulos (Hannibal), Iu.: vestem,…

diductio.definition: dīductiō ōnis, f diduco, a divergence, opposite conclusion : rationis.

diecula.definition: diēcula ae, f dim. dies, a little while, respite , T., C.

dies.definition: diēs gen. diēī or diē (rarely diei, disyl., T., or diī, V.), m sometimes in sing f. DIV-, a day, civil day : Quae tot res in unum conclusit diem, T.: eo die, Cs.: in posterum diem, Cs.: paucos dies ibi morati, Cs.: al…

diffamo.definition: (diffāmō) —, ātus, āre dis- + fama, to make a scandal of, divulge : adulterium diffamatum, O.: prava, Ta.— To malign : viros procacibus scriptis, Ta.

differentia.definition: differentia ae, f differo, a difference, diversity : honesti et decori: in principiis.— A species : (opp. genus).

differo.definition: differō distulī, dīlātus, ferre dis- + fero, to carry apart, spread abroad, scatter, disperse, separate : venti magnitudine ignem, Cs.: Nubila, V.: rudentis (Eurus), H.: in versum ulmos, i. e. planted , V.: Mettum in …

differtus.definition: differtus adj. dis- + farcio, stuffed, crammed, crowded, swarming : provincia differta exactoribus, Cs.: corpus odoribus, Ta.: differtum forum populumque (i. e. forum differtum populo), H.

difficilis.definition: difficilis e, adj. with comp. and sup. dis- + facilis, hard, difficult, troublesome, impracticable, laborious, perilous : res, T.: facilia ex difficillimis redigere, Cs.: opus: locus: in locos difficilī s abire, S.: v…

difficiliter.definition: difficiliter adv. with comp. and sup. difficilis, with difficulty : a vero internosci: difficilius, confieri, Cs.: quae difficillime praecaventur.

difficultas.definition: difficultās ātis (gen plur. -tātium, L.), f difficilis, difficulty, trouble, distress, poverty, want, embarrassment : discendi: navigandi, Cs.: faciundi pontis, Cs.: loci, S.: vecturae: summa navium: rei frumentariae,…

difficulter.definition: difficulter adv. difficilis, with difficulty, hardly : fiebat, Cs.: haud difficulter persuasum Latinis, L.; see difficiliter.

diffidenter.definition: diffīdenter diffidens, distrustfully, diffidently : diffidenter attingere aliquid: agere, L.

diffidentia.definition: diffīdentia ae, f diffidens, mistrust, distrust, diffidence : fidentiae contrarium est: rei, S.: non tam diffidentiā, futura quae imperavisset, quam, etc., S.

diffido.definition: diffīdo fīsus sum, ere dis- + fido, to distrust, be diffident, be distrustful, despair : iacet, diffidit: sui, S.: sibi aliquā ratione: eius fidei: suis rebus, Cs.: exercitui, S.: summae rei, Cs.: armis, V.: cur M. Va…

diffindo.definition: diffindō fidī, fissus, ere dis- + findo, to cleave asunder, split, divide . saxo diffisso: diffissā nate, H.: tempora plumbo, V.: portas muneribus, i. e. to open , H.—Fig., to detract : nihil hinc diffindere possum, c…

diffingo.definition: diffingō —, —, ere dis- + fingo, to transform, remodel, make anew : ferrum incude, H. — Fig.: alqd, alter , H.

diffiteor.definition: diffiteor —, ērī dis + fateor, to disavow, deny : opus, O.

diffluo.definition: diffluō fluxī, —, ere dis- + fluo, to flow in different directions, flow away : in plurīs partīs (Rhenus), branches , Cs.; cf. nos quasi extra ripas diffluentīs coercere.— To be dissolved : iecur, L.: sudore, Ph.— To …

diffugio.definition: diffugiō fūgī, —, ere dis- + fugio, to fly apart, flee in different directions, disperse, scatter : metu perterriti diffugimus: Diffugimus visu exsangues, V.: diffugiunt stellae, O.: nives, disappear , H.: sollicitudi…

diffugium.definition: diffugium ī, n dis + 2 FVG-, a dispersion. —Plur. : proximorum, Ta.

diffundo.definition: diffundō fūdī, fūsus, ere dis- + fundo, to spread by pouring, pour out, pour forth : sanguis in omne corpus diffunditur: tum freta diffundi iussit, O.: vina iterum (consule) Tauro diffusa, bottled , H.: in alqm venenu…

diffuse.definition: diffūsē adv. with comp. diffusus, in a scattered manner : res dictae.— Copiously, fully : dicenda diffusius.

diffusus.definition: diffūsus adj. P. of diffundo, spread abroad, extended, wide : platanus diffusa ramis. — Fig.: ius civile, prolix : vocis genus, protracted .

diffututus.definition: diffutūtus adj., exhausted by indulgence, Ct.

digamma.definition: digamma atis, n , di/gamma, the digamma: tuum, your letter F (for fenus), i. e. your interestbook.

digero.definition: dī-gerō gessī, gestus, ere, to force apart, separate, divide, distribute: In canes totidem digestus Cerberus, O.: Nilus septem in cornua, O.—Poet.: novem volucrīs in belli digerit annos, i. e. interprets to mean years…

digestio.definition: dīgestiō ōnis, f digero, an enumeration .

digitulus.definition: digitulus ī, m dim. digitus, a little finger , T.: aniculae collum digitulis oblidere.

digitus.definition: digitus ī, m DIC-, a finger : de digito anulum detraho, T.: digitos impellere, ut Scriberent: Indice monstrare digito, H.: illam digito uno attingere, to touch gently , T.: alqd extremis digitis attingere, to touch li…

digladior.definition: dī-gladior atus, ārī, dep. gladius, to fight for life and death, contend fiercely : cives inter se sicis. —Fig.: de alquā re: digladientur illi per me licet.

dignatio.definition: dīgnātiō ōnis, f dignor, honor, rank : de dignatione laborat: principum, L.: principis, Ta.

digne.definition: dīgnē adv. with comp. dignus, worthily, fitly, becomingly : laudari satis digne: iniuriam persequi: Martem scribere, H.: Peccare cruce dignius, H.

dignitas.definition: dīgnitās ātis, f dignus, worth, merit, desert, character : tantum apud me dignitas potest, Cs.: honos dignitate impetratus: consularis, a claim to the consulship : pro dignitate laudare.— Greatness, majesty, dignity, …

digno.definition: dīgnō —, —, āre dignus, to deem worthy : cunctas nomine, C. poët.: laude dignari: coniugio Veneris dignate, V.

dignor.definition: dīgnor ātus, ārī, dep. dignus, to deem worthy, honor, deign, condescend : tali me honore, V.: quaecumque (loca) adventu, Ta.: alio te funere, V.: Bis septem ordinibus quam (summam) lex dignatur Othonis, requires for a…

dignus.definition: dīgnus adj. with comp. and sup. DEC-, worthy, deserving, meritorious, deserved, suitable, fitting, becoming, proper : quod te dignumst facere, T.: vir maioribus suis dignissimus: adsentatio, quae ne libero quidem dign…

digredior.definition: dīgredior gressus, ī, dep. dis- + gradior, to go apart, go asunder, separate, part, go away, depart : Hos digrediens adfabar, at parting , V.: dein digrediens, stepping aside , S.: luna tum congrediens cum sole, tum d…

digressio.definition: dīgressiō ōnis, f digredior, a parting, separating : nostra.—Fig., a digression : a propositā oratione.

digressus2.definition: dīgressus ūs, m digredior, a parting, separating, departure : meus: amici, Iu.

dii.definition: diī. 1. Nom. plur. of deus.— 2. Gen. of dies.

diiudicatio.definition: dīiūdicātiō ōnis, f diiudico, a judging, deciding .

diiudico.definition: dī-iūdicō āvī, ātus, āre, to distinguish, know apart, discern, perceive the difference: vera et falsa: vera a falsis: inter has sententias. — To judge, discern, decide, determine: dicam, quod mihi in mentemst, tu diiu…

dilabor.definition: dī-lābor lapsus, ī, dep., to fall asunder, go to pieces, melt away, dissolve: glacies dilapsa: nix, L.: Volcanus (i. e. ignis), H.: Fibrenus, et divisus aequaliter rapideque dilapsus, flowing apart: ungula in quinos d…

dilacero.definition: dī-lacerō āvī, ātus, āre, to tear to pieces, tear apart: dominum, O.: corpus tormentis, Ta.—Fig., to tear to pieces, waste: ad dilacerandam rem p.: opes, O.: acerbitatibus dilaceratus, Ta.

dilanio.definition: dī-laniō āvī, ātus, āre, to tear to pieces, mutilate: (cadaver) canibus dilaniandum: alqm tormentis, Ta.: membra, O.

dilapido.definition: dī-lapidō —, —, āre, to throw away, squander, consume: triginta minas, T.

dilargior.definition: dī-largior ītus, īrī, dep., to give liberally, lavish: omnia quibus voluit: foedera sociis, Ta.

dilatio.definition: dīlātiō ōnis, f dis- + TAL-, a putting off, postponement, delay : vel minime temporis: comitiorum: nulla, L.: per dilationes bellum geri, L.

dilato.definition: dīlātō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. dilatus, to spread out, dilate, broaden, stretch, enlarge, extend : manum: fundum: castra, L.: rictūs, O. — Fig., to spread, amplify, dilate, extend : orationem: haec: gloriam: litteras, t…

dilator.definition: dīlātor ōris, m dis- + TAL-, a delayer, dilatory person , H.

dilaudo.definition: dī-laudō to distinguish by praise, eulogize: libros.

dilectus1.definition: dīlēctus adj. P. of diligo, loved, beloved, dear : Maecenas, H.: Superis, O.: sorori, V.

dilectus2.definition: dīlēctus or dēlēctus ū s, m dis- or dē + 1 LEG-, a choosing, picking out, selecting, selection, choice, distinction : ad quod delectus adhibetur: iudicum: dignitatis: non dilectu aliquo ducitur ad iudicandum: sine ull…

diligens.definition: dīligēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of diligo, industrious, careful, assiduous, attentive, diligent, accurate, scrupulous, faithful : diligentissimi aratores: homo, thrifty : servi: in re hereditariā: in osten…

diligenter.definition: dīligenter adv. with comp. and sup. diligens, industriously, attentively, diligently, assiduously : iter facere, Cs.: omnia agere: percipite quae dicam: diligentius (libelli) sunt reconditi: quos diligentissime conser…

diligentia.definition: dīligentia ae, f diligens, attentiveness, earnestness, diligence, industry, assiduity, care, faithfulness : non mediocrem diligentiam adhibere, Cs.: summa in re p.: erga pecuniam, Ta.: vostra, T.: quā diligentiā fueri…

diligo.definition: dīligō lēxī, lēctus, ere dis- + 2 lego, to single out, value, esteem, prize, love : alqm: se ipse: inter se: civitates eum diligebant, Cs.: magno dilectus amore, V.: Lalage, Dilecta quantum, etc., H.: te in fratris lo…

dilorico.definition: dī-lōrīcō —, ātus, āre, to tear open: tunicam.

diluceo.definition: dī-lūceō —, —, ēre, to be clear, be evident: dilucere id quod erat coepit, L.: res patribus, L.

dilucesco.definition: dīlūcēscō lūxī, —, ere, inch. diluceo, to grow light, begin to shine, dawn : Omnem crede diem tibi diluxisse supremum, H.—Impers: cum iam dilucesceret: iam dilucescebat, cum, etc., L.: diluxit.

dilucide.definition: dīlūcidē adv. dilucidus, plainly, evidently, distinctly : expedire Iudicibus, T.: explicare: respondeo.

dilucidus.definition: dīlūcidus adj. with comp. diluceo, clear, distinct, evident : oratio: omnia dilucidiora facientes.

diluculum.definition: dīlūculum ī, n diluceo, daybreak, dawn .

diludium.definition: dīlūdium ī, n dis + ludus, a resting-time, intermission.—Plur ., H.

diluo.definition: dī-luō uī, ūtus, ere, to wash away, dissolve, dilute, wash, drench: ne aqua lateres diluere posset, Cs.: sata laeta, V.: unguenta lacrimis, O.: diluta labella guttis, moistened, Ct.— To dissolve, temper, dilute, mix, …

dilutus.definition: dīlūtus adj. P. of diluo, thin, weak, dilute .— Comp.: dilutius poturi (sc. vinum).

diluvies.definition: dīluviēs —, acc. em, f diluo, an inundation, flood, deluge : fera, H.

diluvium.definition: dīluvium ī, n diluo, an inundation, flood, deluge : Diluvio miscens (tellurem), V., O.—Fig., desolation, destruction : illud, V., Iu.

dimachae.definition: dimachae ārum, m , dima/xai, mounted infantry, dragoons, Cu.

dimano.definition: dī-mānō āvī, —, āre, to spread abroad: ad existimationem hominum latius.

dimensio.definition: dīmēnsiō ōnis, f dis- + 1 MA-, a measuring : quadrati.

dimetior.definition: dī-mētior mēnsus, īrī, dep. and pass, to measure, measure out, lay out: syllabas: caelum atque terram: campum ad certamen, V.: positūs siderum, Ta.: digitis peccata sua, to count off.—Pass., to be measured, be planned…

dimetor.definition: dī-mētor (dē-) ātus, ārī, dep. and pass. —Dep., to measure out, mark out: eorum cursū s dimetati cognovimus.—Pass, to be measured out, be marked: locum castris dimetari iussit, L.: dimetata signa (al. demetata).

dimicatio.definition: dīmicātiō ōnis, f dimico, a fight, combat, struggle, encounter : maxima, Cs.: bellum ingenti dimicatione geritur, L.: priorum dimicationum fructus, Cs.: proelii: universae rei, a general engagement , L. — A combating,…

dimico.definition: dī-micō āvī (dīmicuisse, O.), ātus, āre, to fight, struggle, contend: armis, Cs.: armis cum aliquo, N.: pro suā quisque patriā ferro, L.: in acie, in the open field, Cs.: equitatu, N.: pro te: ancipiti proelio dimicat…

dimidiatus.definition: dīmidiātus adj. dimidium, halved, divided in the middle : mensis: partes versiculorum.

dimidium.definition: dīmidium ī, n dimidius, the half : Vix dum dimidium dixeram, was hardly half through , T.: ut ne minus dimidium ad illum perveniret: quos dimidio redderet stultiores, by half : Hibernia dimidio minor quam, etc., Cs.: …

dimidius.definition: dīmidius adj. dis- + medius, half, one half : pro dimidiā parte: rex dimidiae partis Eburonum, Cs.—Fig., of descent: dimidius patrum, dimidius plebis, half patrician and half plebeian , L.— Broken in two, broken : cru…

dimissio.definition: dīmissiō ōnis, f dimitto, a sending out, sending forth : libertorum ad provincias.— A dismissing, discharge : propugnatorum.

dimissus2.definition: (dīmissus ūs), m a deliverance. — Only dat: hanc quaestionem dimissui sperant futuram (dub.).

dimitto.definition: dī-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to send different ways, send out, send forth, send about, scatter, distribute: litteras circum municipia, Cs.: litteras per provincias, Cs.: certos per litora, V.: nuntios totā civitate Aed…

dimminuo.definition: dimminuō —, —, ere dis- + minuo, to break to pieces, shatter, break : tibi caput, T.: Dimminuetur tibi cerebrum, T.

dimoveo.definition: dī-moveō ōvī, ōtus, ēre, to move asunder, part, put asunder, separate, divide: terram aratro, V.: glaebas aratro, O.: auras, V.: cinerem foco, O.: rubum, i. e. creep through, H. — To separate, disperse, scatter, dismi…

dinosco.definition: dī-nōscō —, —, ere, to know apart, distinguish, discern: vera bona, Iu.: (geminos) inter se similes, O.: civem hoste, H.: dominum et servum deliciis, Ta.: curvo rectum, H.

dinumeratio.definition: dīnumerātiō ōnis, f dinumero, a counting over, reckoning up, enumeration : noctium ac dierum.—As a figure of speech, C.

dinumero.definition: dī-numerō āvī, ātus, are, to count, reckon, enumerate, compute: stellas regis annos: tempora, V.: generis gradūs, O.—To count out, pay: viginti minas, T.

dioecesis.definition: dioecēsis is, f , dioi/khsis, a governor's jurisdiction, district.

dioecetes.definition: dioecētēs ae, m , dioikhth/s, an overseer of the revenue, royal treasurer.

diota.definition: diōta ae, f, = * diw/th two-eared, a twohandled vessel, wine-jar, H.

diploma.definition: diplōma atis, n di/plwma, a letter of recommendation, letter of authority, C., Ta.

dira1.definition: (dīra ae), f dirus, a bad omen (only plur.): dirae, sicut cetera auspicia, etc.— A curse, execration : Diris agam vos, H.: compositae, Ta.

directe.definition: dīrēctē adv. with comp. dirigo, in a straight line, precisely, exactly : ad perpendiculum, Cs.: directius gubernare: dicere.

diremptus2.definition: dīrēmptus ūs, m dirimo, a separation .

direptio.definition: dīreptiō ōnis, f diripio, a plundering, pillaging, sack : sociorum: fanorum: urbis, Cs. — Plur: aratorum.

direptor.definition: dīreptor ōris, m diripio, a plunderer : urbis.

diribeo.definition: diribeō —, itus, ēre dis- + habeo, to separate, sort, canvass (ballots): dum de te tabellae diribeantur: diribitae tabellae.

diribitio.definition: diribitiō ōnis, f diribeo, a separation, sorting, canvass (of ballots).

diribitor.definition: diribitor ōris, m a sorter, canvasser (of ballots): tabellarum.

dirigo1.definition: dīrigō rēxī, rēctus, ere dis- + rego, to distribute, scatter : volnera (i. e. tela), V.— To lay out, arrange in lines : regiones urbis: vicos, i. e. the rows of houses , L.

dirimo.definition: dirimō ēmī, ēmptus, ere dis- + emo, to take apart, part, separate, divide, cut off : dirimi (corpus) distrahive: dirimit Suebiam montium iugum, Ta.: urbs flumine dirempta, L.: a continenti urbem, Cu.: si quem dirimit …

diripio.definition: dīripiō uī, eptus, ere dis- + rapio, to tear asunder, tear in pieces : Cum diripereris equis, O.: membra manibus nefandis, O.: dapes, V.— To lay waste, ravage, spoil, plunder, pillage : bona eorum, Cs.: oppidum, Cs.: …

diritas.definition: dīritās ātis, f dirus, mischief, misfortune, calamity : invecta casu, C. poët.— Fierceness, cruelty : omni diritate taeterrimus: quanta in alquo.

dirumpo.definition: dī-rumpō or dis-rumpō rūpī, ruptus, ere, to break to pieces, break, shatter: partem (nubis): homo diruptus, that has a rupture: dirupi me paene, nearly bursts my lungs: Disrumpor, T.: disrumparis licet: plausu dirumpi…

diruo.definition: dī-ruō ruī, rutus, ere, to tear asunder, overthrow, demolish, destroy: maceriam iube dirui, T.: urbem: muros, N.: nova diruunt, alia aedificant, S.: post diruta Pergama, O.—To scatter, disperse, destroy: agmina vasto …

dirus.definition: dīrus adj. with comp, ill - omened, ominous, boding, portentous, fearful, awful, dread: cometae, V.: quibus nihil dirius: mortalibus omen, O.: tempus: exsecratio, L. — Plur n. as subst: in dira incurrimus: Dira canere…

dis1.definition: dīs dītis, neut. dīte, adj. with comp. dītior and sup. dītissimus DIV-, rich, wealthy, opulent, provided, abounding : dis quidem esses, T.: Cratini huius ditis aedes, T.: domus, H.: patre diti, N.: Mycenae, H.: delubr…

discedo.definition: dis-cēdō cessī, cessus, ere, to go apart, part asunder, divide, separate, disperse, scatter : ex hac fugā auxilia discesserunt, Cs.: lignationis causā in silvas, Cs.: ut sodalitates decuriatique discederent: cum disce…

disceptatio.definition: disceptātiō ōnis, f discepto, a dispute, disputation, debate, discussion, disquisition : cum quibus omnis nobis disceptatio est: (causa) in disceptatione versata: privata: illa disceptatio tenebat, quod, etc., the poi…

disceptator.definition: disceptātor ōris, m discepto, an umpire, arbitrator, judge : criminis: populo R. disceptatore uti: de suo iure ad Caesarem disceptatorem venire, Cs.: inter patrem et filium, L.

disceptatrix.definition: disceptātrīx īcis, f disceptator, an arbitrator : dialectica veri et falsi.

discepto.definition: disceptō āvī, ātus, āre dis- + capto, to decide, determine, judge, arbitrate, sit as umpire : haec iuste: causam in foro dicere disceptante te: exercitu disceptante, L.: inter populum et regem in re praesenti, L.: eor…

discerno.definition: dis-cernō crēvī, crētus, ere, to separate, set apart, mark off, bound, part, divide: muro di scerni a nobis: discrimina, quibus ordines discernerentur, L.: mons, qui finī s eorum discerneret, S.— Poet.: (saxum) telas …

discerpo.definition: discerpō psī, ptus, ere dis- + carpo, to tear in pieces, rend, mangle, mutilate : animus nec dividi nec discerpi potest: discerptum regem manibus, L.: membra gruis, H.—Poet.: aurae Omnia discerpunt, scatter , V. — Fig…

discessio.definition: discessiō ōnis, f discedo, a separation, division : Si eveniat discessio, a divorce , T.—Of the senate, a division, formal vote : senatus consultum de supplicatione per discessionem fecit: sine ullā varietate, a unani…

discessus2.definition: discessus ūs, m dis- + 1 CAD-, a going asunder, parting : non longinquus inter nos: caeli, i. e. lightning.—A going away, departure, removal , withdrawal : tuus:. ab urbe: e vitā: latronis: meus, banishment : discessu…

discidium.definition: dīscidium ī, n dis- + 2 SAC-, a parting, separation, disagreement, dissension, discord : inter nos, T.: nil, quod sit discidio dignum, divorce , T.: cupido Si tibi discidii est, O.: manente memoriā in discidio foederu…

discinctus.definition: discinctus adj. P. of discingo, ungirt, without the girdle : discincti ludere, in loose dress , i. e. at ease , H.— Voluptuous, effeminate, dissolute : Afri, V.: nepos, H.

discindo.definition: dī-scindō cidī, cissus, ere, to tear asunder, cut apart, cleave, divide, rend, tear: Vestem, T.: tunicam: purpureos amictūs manu, V.: labrum, T.: artūs, V.: novaculā cotem, L.: amicitiae discindendae, rudely broken off.

discingo.definition: dis-cingō nxī, nctus, ere, to ungird, deprive of the girdle: centuriones discinctos destitui iussit, i. e. to lose their mantles, L.: discinctā tunicā, H.: Afros, i. e. strip utterly, Iu.: neque ego discingor, i. e. r…

disciplina.definition: disciplīna ae, f discipulus, instruction, tuition, teaching, training, education : puerilis: adulescentīs in disciplinam ei tradere: te in disciplinam meam tradere: in disciplinam (Druidum) convenire, Cs.: res, quarum…

discipula.definition: discipula ae, f discipulus, a female scholar, disciple , H.

discipulus.definition: discipulus ī, m disco, a learner, scholar, pupil, disciple, student, follower : Num immemores discipuli? Have the pupils forgotten (their lesson)? T.: Platonis: laboris et fori.

discludo.definition: disclūdō sī, sus, ere dis + claudo, to keep apart, divide, shut off : Nerea ponto, V.: quibus (tignis) disclusis, held asunder , Cs.: iram et cupiditatem locis, to assign : morsūs roboris, relax the pinch , V.

disco.definition: discō didicī, —, ere DIC-, to learn, learn to know, acquire, become acquainted with : litteras: ius civile: dialectica ab aliquo: id de me, T.: virtutem ex me, V.: quae illi litteris, ego militando didici, S.: per lab…

discolor.definition: dis-color ōris, adj., of another color, not of the same color: auri per ramos aura, V.: matrona meretrici, different in dress, H.: vestis fatis discolor alba meis, O.—Party-colored, of different colors: signa: miles, …

disconvenio.definition: dis-conveniō —, —, īre, to disagree, be inconsistent: vitae ordine toto, H.—Impers: eo disconvenit inter Meque et te, H.

discordia.definition: discordia ae, f discors, disunion, disagreement, dissension, variance, discord : confingis causas ad discordiam, T.: civilis, S.: facultas discordiae concitandae: duas ex unā civitate discordia fecerat, L.: perfecta t…

discordiosus.definition: discordiōsus adj. discordia, full of discord, intractable, quarrelsome : volgus, S.

discordo.definition: discordō —, —, āre discors, to be at variance, differ, quarrel : inter se, T.: cupiditates in animis discordant: animus secum discordans: patria, Ta.—Poet., to be unlike, be opposed : quantum discordet parcus avaro, H…

discors.definition: dis-cors cordis, adj. dis + cor.—Of persons, discordant, disagreeing, inharmonious, at variance : homines ambitione: ad alia discordes in uno consentire, L.: gens, L.—Poet.: Tanais discors, i. e. the Parthians , H.: f…

discrepantia.definition: discrepantia ae, f discrepo, discordance, dissimilarity, discrepancy : rerum, verborum.

discrepatio.definition: discrepātiō ōnis, f discrepo, a disagreement, dispute : inter consules, L.

discrepo.definition: dis-crepō uī, —, āre, to differ in sound, be discordant, fail to harmonize: (fides) paulum.—Fig., to disagree, be inconsistent, be different, vary, differ, be at odds: si quid discrepet: quae inter conlegas discrepare…

discribo.definition: dī-scrībō scrīpsī, scrīptus, ere, to distribute, divide, apportion, assign: (argentum) illis, T.: civitatibus pecuniarum summas: urbis partīs ad incendia: duodena in singulos homines iugera: pretio iura: Sedes discrip…

discrimen.definition: discrīmen inis, n dis- + 2 CER-, that which parts, an intervening space, interval, distance, division, separation : cum (maria) pertenui discrimine separarentur: discrimina costis spina dabat, parted , V.: finem atque…

discrimino.definition: discrīminō āvī, ātus, āre discrimen, to divide, part, separate : Etruriam discriminat Cassia: late agros, V.: vigiliarum somnique tempora, apportion , L.

discriptio.definition: dīscrīptiō ōnis, f discribo, a division, distribution, apportionment, assignment : civitatis: populi: possessionum: per urbem caedis (cf. descriptio).

discrucio.definition: dis-cruciō —, ātus, āre, to rack to pieces, torture.—Only pass: Brutum, Cassium discruciatos necare: Discrucior animi, am distracted, T.: discrucior, fundum a Curtilio possideri.

discumbo.definition: discumbō cubuī, cubitus, ere CVB-, to lie down, recline at table : discubuimus omnes, took our places : toris pictis, V.: discumbere iussus, invited to dinner , Iu.: discumbitur.— To lie down to sleep : cenati discubu…

discupio.definition: dis-cupiō —, —, ere, to desire greatly, long: se vendere, Ct.

discurro.definition: dis-currō currī and cucurrī, cursus, ere, to run different ways, run to and fro, run about, wander, roam: in muris armata civitas, Cs.: deus in montibus altis, O.: circa vias, L.: per omnīs silvas, O.: Olli discurrēre…

discursus2.definition: discursus ūs, m discurro, a running to and fro, running about, straggling : continere ab discursu militem, L.: vallem discursibus impleat, O.: subito discursu, a double flank movement , Ta.

discus.definition: discus ī, m , di/skos, a quoit: pete cedentem aëra disco, H.: Indoctus disci, H.: discum audire quam philosophum malunt.

discutio.definition: discutiō cussī, cussus, ere dis + quatio, to strike asunder, dash to pieces, shatter : columna ad imum fulmine discussa est, L.: arietibus aliquantum muri, L.: latericium, Cs.: tempora ictu, O.: nubīs, O.: discussae i…

diserte.definition: disertē adv. with sup. disertus, clearly, eloquently, expressly : hoc scribere: disertissime scriptum, L.

disertus.definition: disertus adj. with comp. and sup. for * dissertus; P. of dissero, skilful, clear, clever, wellspoken, fluent : homo, T.: disertos cognosse me nonnullos: adulescens: ad vinum: calices quem non fecere disertum? H.: laud…

disicio.definition: dīsiciō or dissiciō (disiicio), iēcī, iectus, ere dis + iacio, to throw asunder, drive asunder, scatter, disperse, break up, tear to pieces : late disiectis moenibus, L.: disiecta spatio urbs, L.: nubīs, O.: ostendens…

disiuncte.definition: (disiūnctē) adv. disiūnctus, separately, without connection .—Only comp: disiunctius dici.

disiunctio.definition: disiūnctiō or dīiūnctiō ōnis, f disiungo, a separation : meorum.— A variation, deviation : animorum: sententiae.— A logical opposition .— In rhet., asyndeton, a succession of clauses without connectives .

disiunctus.definition: disiūnctus (dīiūnc-) adj. with comp. and sup. P. of disiungo, parted, separate, distant, remote : disiunctissimae terrae: Aetolia procul a barbaris disiuncta gentibus.—Fig., apart, different, remote, disconnected, str…

disiungo.definition: dis-iungō or dīiungō ūnxī, ūnctus, ere, to unyoke: iumenta: bos disiunctus, H.: fessos iuvencos, O. — To disunite, sever, divide, separate, part, remove: (fons) munitione diiunctus a mari: Iugurthae Bocchique regnum (…

disor.definition: dis- or dī- praep., inseparable DVA-, disbefore c, p, q, s, t , dī- before d, g, l, m, n, r , and v (but usu. dimminuō, sometimes disrumpo), dif- before f Before a vowel dis- becomes dir-; before i consonant, sometime…

dispalatus.definition: dis-pālātus adj., straggling, astray: in agris, N.: multitudo, N.

dispar.definition: dis-pār aris, adj., unlike, dissimilar, different, unequal, ill-matched: dispares mores disparia studia sequentur: pari gratiā sed genere dispari, Cs.: certabant, ipsi pares, ceterum opibus disparibus, S.: rebus et or…

disparatum.definition: disparātum ī, n disparo.—In rhet., a direct opposition .

disparilis.definition: dis-parilis e, adj., dissimilar, different: adspiratio terrarum.

disparo.definition: dis-parō āvī, ātus, āre, to part, separate, divide: eos disparandos curavit, Cs.: (classīs) ita ut, etc.

dispello.definition: dis-pellō pulī, pulsus, ere, to drive asunder, scatter, disperse: pecudes dispulsae: per undas nos, V.: alquos aequore turbo, V.—Fig., to drive away, dispel: sole dispulsa nebula, L.: ab animo caliginem: tenebras calu…

dispendium.definition: dispendium ī, n dispendo, expense, cost, loss : sine suo dispendio, T.—Plur, Pr.—Fig.: morae, loss of time , V.

dispensatio.definition: dispēnsātiō ōnis, f dispenso, management, charge, direction, superintendence, provision, stewardship : aerari: annonae, L.: inopiae, Cs.: regia.

dispensator.definition: dispēnsātor ōris, m dispenso, a steward, attendant, treasurer , C.: dispensatore Armigero, Iu.

dispenso.definition: dispēnsō āvī, ātus, āre, to disburse, pay out: qui dispensat, the steward, Iu.: alquem eligere ad dispensandam pecuniam, as paymaster, N. — To distribute, dispense, share: oscula suprema natos per omnīs, O.: inventa i…

disperdo.definition: dis-perdō didī, —, ere, to spoil, ruin: possessiones: carmen, V.: me (puella), O.

dispereo.definition: dis-pereō iī, —, īre, to go to ruin, be undone, perish: fundum populi R. disperire pati: tui labores, Ct.—Esp. colloq., in exclamations: disperii, perii misera, it's all over with me, T.: dispeream, ni Summosses omnīs…

dispergo.definition: dīspergō or dīspargō sī , sus, ere dis- + spargo, to scatter, spread abroad, disperse : tibi cerebrum, T.: per agros passim corpus: membrorum collectio dispersa: dispersa inmittit silvis incendia, V.: quae (duo milia …

disperse.definition: dīspersē adv. dispersus, here and there, occasionally : dictae res: multis in locis dicta.

dispersio.definition: dīspersiō ōnis, f dispergo, a destruction : urbis (dub.).

dispertio.definition: dispertiō īvī, ītus, īre dis- + partio, to distribute, divide : inter manipulos funditores, S.: pecuniam iudicibus: exercitum per oppida, L.: mensam servis, N.: portas tribunis, assign , S.— Fig., to divide, apportion…

dispertior.definition: dispertior —, īrī, dep. dis- + partior, to distribute, apportion : belli administrationem inter se, L.: alqd in infinitum, i. e. refine .

dispertitio.definition: dispertītiō ōnis, f dispertio, a destruction : urbis (dub.).

dispicio.definition: dīspiciō spēxī, spectus, ere SPEC-, to descry, discern, perceive, make out, distinguish, detect (by the sight): ne scintillam quidem ullam ad dispiciendum reliquerunt: acie mentis: catuli, qui iam dispecturi sunt: sum…

displiceo.definition: displiceō uī, itus, ēre dis- + placeo, to displease, be unsatisfactory : mihi: si displicebit vita, T.: verbum vehementer displicet, I dislike extremely : mihi non displicet (propulsare, etc.), I am inclined : totus d…

displodo.definition: (dis-plōdō) —, ōsus, ere, to burst, cause to explode.—Only p. perf.: displosa vesica, H.

dispono.definition: dis-pōnō posuī, positus, ere, to place here and there, array, distribute, set in order, arrange, dispose: Homeri libros: ordines in quincuncem, Cs.: comas, O.: ensīs per herbam, V. — In military operations, to set in …

disposite.definition: dispositē adv. dispositus, orderly, methodically : accusare istum.

dispositio.definition: dispositiō ōnis, f dispono, a regular disposition, arrangement : argumentorum.

dispositus2.definition: (dispositus ūs), m a disposition, arrangement.—Only abl sing.: civilium rerum, Ta.

dispudet.definition: dis-pudet —, ēre, impers, it shames, is shameful: Sic mihi data esse verba, T.

disputatio.definition: disputātiō ōnis, f disputo, an argument, discussion, debate, dispute : magis facilis quam necessaria: isti disputationi nihil est loci: in utramque partem, Cs.—Plur., C.

disputator.definition: disputātor ōris, m disputo, a disputer, disputant : subtilis.

disputo.definition: dis-putō āvī, ātus, āre, to weigh, examine, investigate, treat, discuss, explain: de singulis sententiis breviter: ad id: multa de sideribus, Cs.: de omni re in contrarias partes: esse in utramque partem disputatum, C…

disquiro.definition: disquīrō —, —, ere dis- + quaero, to inquire diligently, investigate : mecum, H.

disquisitio.definition: disquīsītiō ōnis, f disquiro, an inquiry, investigation : in magnis disquisitionibus: in disquisitionem venit, ne, etc., L.

dissaepio.definition: dis-saepiō (not -sēpiō), psī, ptus, ere, to part off, separate, divide: limitibus omnia certis, O.— Fig.: tenui muro alqd.

dissemino.definition: dis-sēminō āvī, ātus, āre, to spread abroad, disseminate: omnia in memoriam sempiternam: malum.

dissensio.definition: dissēnsiō ōnis, f dissentio, difference of opinion, disagreement, dissension, discord, strife : regum, S.: inter eos magna: parva est mihi tecum dissensio?: amicorum disiunctio dissensionem facit: alqd dissensionis co…

dissensus2.definition: (dissēnsus ūs), m dissentio, dissension, disagreement .—Only abl sing. : vario, V.

dissentaneus.definition: dissentāneus adj. dissentio, disagreeing, contrary : alcui rei.

dissentio.definition: dis-sentiō sēnsī, sēnsus, īre, to differ, dissent, disagree, be at odds, contradict, quarrel: a te dissentiens senator: ab iudicio omnium: in hoc: a ceterarum gentium more: inter se: qui dissentiunt: nisi quid tu Diss…

disserenasco.definition: (disserēnāscō) āvī, —, āre, inch impers. dis + sereno, to clear up, grow clear : cum undique disserenasset, L.

dissero1.definition: dis-serō —, —, ere, to plant here and there: taleae intermissis spatiis disserebantur, Cs.

dissero2.definition: dis-serō ruī, rtus, ere, to examine, argue, discuss, speak, harangue, discourse, treat: mecum: pluribus verbis sit disserendum: philosophiae pars, quae est disserendi: de omnibus rebus in contrarias partīs: pro legibu…

dissertio.definition: dissertiō ōnis, f 2 dissero, a gradual destruction, abolition : iuris humani, L. (dub.).

disserto.definition: dissertō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. dissero, to discuss, debate, treat : vim Romanam, Ta.: rectius de alquā re, Ta.

dissideo.definition: dissideō ēdī, —, ēre dis- + sedeo, to sit apart, be remote : sceptris quae (terra) libera nostris Dissidet, V.: quantum Hypanis dissidet Eridano, Pr. — Fig., to be at variance, disagree, differ : non consiliis, sed ar…

dissignatio.definition: dissīgnātiō ōnis, f dissigno, an arrangement (v. l. for designatio).

dissignator.definition: dissīgnātor (not dēsīg-), ōris, m dissigno, an undertaker, manager (at a funeral), H.

dissigno.definition: dis-sīgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to unseal, disclose: Quid non ebrietas dissignat? H. — Fig., to arrange, dispose, regulate, set in order (only v. l. for designo).

dissilio.definition: dissiliō uī, —, īre dis- + salio, to leap asunder, fly apart, burst, break up, split : mucro ictu dissiluit, V.: aera (sc. frigore), V.: Haec loca convolsa ruinā Dissiluisse ferunt, V.: Caput dissilire neniā, H.—Fig.,…

dissimilis.definition: dis-similis e, adj. with comp. and sup, unlike, dissimilar, different: duo dissimilia genera, lenonum et latronum: dissimilis est militum causa et tua: hac in re unā Multum dissimiles, H.: quod est non dissimile atque…

dissimiliter.definition: dissimiliter adv. dissimilis, differently, in a different manner : efficere voluptates: oppidum situm, S.: haud dissimiliter navibus vagis, L.

dissimilitudo.definition: dissimilitūdō inis, f dissimilis, unlikeness, difference, dissimilitude : temporis: studiorum.

dissimulanter.definition: dissimulanter adv. dissimulo, dissemblingly, secretly : verba conclusa: adservari, L.

dissimulantia.definition: dissimulantia ae, f dissimulo, a dissembling .

dissimulatio.definition: dissimulātiō ōnis, f dissimulo, a disguising : sui, Ta.— A dissembling, concealment, dissimulation : dissimulatione tecta improbitas: cupiditatis, irony .

dissimulator.definition: dissimulātor ōris, m dissimulo, a dissembler, concealer : alcuius rei, S.: opis propriae, of my own influence , H.: amoris, O.: alienae culpae, Ta.

dissimulo.definition: dis-simulō āvī, ātus, āre, to make unlike, disguise: tauro dissimulante deum, concealing the divinity, O.: se, to assume another form, O.: capillos Dissimulant plumae, i. e. take the place of, O.—To dissemble, hide, c…

dissipabilis.definition: dissipābilis e, adj. dissipo, that may be dispersed : ignis et aër.

dissipatio.definition: dissipātiō ōnis, f dissipo, a scattering, dispersing : civium: praedae, i. e. plundering.—Destruction, annihilation : corporum. — In rhet., the use of contrasted adverbs of place in parallel clauses .

dissipatus.definition: dissipātus adj. P. of dissipo, scattering, incoherent : oratio: dissipata conectere: in instruendo (orator).

dissipo.definition: dissipō or dissupō āvī, ātus, āre dis + * supo, throw, to spread abroad, scatter, disperse : ignis se dissipavit, L.: fratris membra: dissipatos homines congregare: venenum per ossa, O.: in mille curias dissipata res …

dissociabilis.definition: dissociābilis e, adj. dissocio, separating, dividing : Oceanus, H.— Irreconcilable : res, Ta.

dissociatio.definition: dissociātiō ōnis, f dissocio, a separation : spiritūs corporisque, Ta.

dissocio.definition: dis-sociō āvī, ātus, āre, to put out of union, disjoin, disunite: Dissociata locis concordi pace ligavit, O.: montes ni dissocientur opacā Valle, H.—Fig., to separate in sentiment, disunite, set at variance, estrange:…
